levels.architect: The scope is assigned automatically to a [[search-scope-display-group]]. Compare it with the [[contextual-search-scope]], which is added to a query to restrict it to a site or list.

terms.summary: The default search scope is the search area used automatically if nobody picks another one.

levels.beginner: The default user store is the first place that search looks to work out who belongs to which group.
levels.maker: It is a [[user-store]] supplied as a starting point for expanding group membership when no user store has been named. It is used by FAST Search Authorization.
levels.architect: FAST Search Authorization uses it when a [[user-store]] is not already specified, as the starting point for expanding group membership.

terms.summary: The default user store is the first place that search looks to work out who belongs to which group.

levels.beginner: A deployment system object is a standard item that is automatically created along with a new site, such as its default home page.
levels.maker: It is an object created as part of a site or site collection. Examples are root folders, catalogs, default pages and galleries created during site or site collection creation.
levels.architect: These objects are part of the site or [[site-collection]] itself, not of a template, so a [[site-template]] does not carry them with it.

terms.summary: A deployment system object is a standard item that is automatically created along with a new site, such as its default home page.

levels.beginner: A descendant content type is a child that inherits from a parent, the way a family recipe is adapted for a new dish.
levels.maker: It is any [[content-type]] that inherits from another content type. Changes to the parent can flow down to the descendants.
levels.architect: Inheritance means that a descendant starts with the settings of its parent. Plan the hierarchy carefully, since many content types can descend from the same one.

terms.summary: A descendant content type is a child that inherits from a parent, the way a family recipe is adapted for a new dish.

levels.beginner: A desktop flow copies the clicks and typing a person would do on a computer, so a repetitive task, like copying details between two old programs, can run on its own.
levels.maker: Desktop flows automate Windows applications and websites, which helps when a system has no [[connector]]. They can run while someone watches (attended) or on their own (unattended), and a [[cloud-flow]] can start them.
levels.architect: Desktop flows run on a Windows machine that is registered to an [[environment]], so you manage the machine, its sessions and its credentials. Automating a screen is more fragile than calling an API, so prefer a [[connector]] when one exists.

terms.summary: A desktop flow copies the clicks and typing a person would do on a computer, so a repetitive task, like copying details between two old programs, can run on its own.

levels.beginner: A document library is the place on a SharePoint site where you store, share and work on files together. It keeps earlier versions of each file and controls who can open or change it.
levels.maker: Libraries add columns (information about each file), views, version history, check-out and co-authoring. Prefer columns and views over deep folder trees, because they make files easier to find and filter. You can sync a library to your computer, and it can use [[content-type|content types]] to describe different kinds of documents.
levels.architect: A library is a list with the DocumentLibrary base template, and each file is a list item with properties. It is reachable through the SharePoint REST API, Microsoft Graph drives and CSOM. Permissions can be inherited or broken at library, folder or item level, but unique permissions are costly at scale. The list view threshold of 5,000 items affects queries and views, and a list or library can hold up to 30 million items.

terms.summary: A document library is the place on a SharePoint site where you store, share and work on files together. It keeps earlier versions of each file and controls who can open or change it.

levels.beginner: Document Processing for Microsoft 365 is a group of AI features that help read, sort and pull information out of documents stored in places such as SharePoint, so people do less manual filing.
levels.maker: Typical uses are classifying documents, extracting details such as dates and amounts from documents like invoices and contracts into columns of a [[document-library]], and starting a follow-up process. It has been known as Microsoft Syntex and as Microsoft Syntex & SharePoint Premium, so older articles use those names. Check which features need extra licences before you plan around them.
levels.architect: The features act on content in SharePoint libraries and write what they find into columns, which other tools can then search, filter and automate on. Treat accuracy as something to measure on your own documents, and confirm per-feature availability and billing for your tenant.

terms.summary: Document Processing for Microsoft 365 is a group of AI features that help read, sort and pull information out of documents stored in places such as SharePoint, so people do less manual filing.

levels.beginner: A draft is a first version written by AI that you are meant to read and improve.
levels.maker: Think of it as a head start. You check it, fix it and make it yours before it goes out.
levels.architect: Calling output a draft is a [[human-in-the-loop]] control: a person remains accountable for what is sent, signed or published.

terms.summary: A draft is a first version written by AI that you are meant to read and improve.

levels.beginner: Dynamic grounding means the AI looks up the latest facts at the moment you ask, instead of using only what it already knew.
levels.maker: This helps answers reflect today's files, messages or web pages rather than old training knowledge.
levels.architect: Retrieval happens at request time, so results depend on [[freshness]] of the index and on permissions. It differs from static instructions that are fixed in the agent's setup.

terms.summary: Dynamic grounding means the AI looks up the latest facts at the moment you ask, instead of using only what it already knew.

levels.beginner: Dynamic rank is how well a search result matches the words you typed, and it changes with every search.
levels.maker: It is the part of an item's rank that depends on how well the query text matches the indexed item. A different query gives a different dynamic rank for the same item. Compare it with [[static-rank]].
levels.architect: The component depends on the match between the query text and the indexed item. It is contrasted with [[static-rank]] and [[query-independent-rank]], which do not vary with the query.

terms.summary: Dynamic rank is how well a search result matches the words you typed, and it changes with every search.

levels.beginner: eDiscovery is how organisations find and collect electronic information for legal or investigation needs.
levels.maker: Compliance teams use it to search, hold and review email, files and chats. This can include content created with Copilot, depending on the service.
levels.architect: The capability is part of [[microsoft-purview]]. Retention, holds and audit settings decide what can be found, so align them with legal requirements.

terms.summary: eDiscovery is how organisations find and collect electronic information for legal or investigation needs.

levels.beginner: An embedding is a list of numbers that captures the meaning of some text, so a computer can tell what is similar.
levels.maker: It is how a search can find a document about "holiday" when you typed "vacation". The meanings sit close together.
levels.architect: A model converts content into a [[vector]]; similarity is then measured mathematically. Embeddings power [[vector-search]] and [[semantic-index|semantic indexes]], and should be created and queried with the same model.

terms.summary: An embedding is a list of numbers that captures the meaning of some text, so a computer can tell what is similar.

levels.beginner: Enterprise data protection is the set of safeguards that keeps your prompts and answers within your organisation's protections.
levels.maker: It applies to eligible work AI experiences and helps ensure the organisation's information is handled under its enterprise terms and controls.
levels.architect: The protections apply to specific products and configurations, so verify coverage per feature. Related earlier names appear under [[microsoft-365-copilot-chat]].

terms.summary: Enterprise data protection is the set of safeguards that keeps your prompts and answers within your organisation's protections.

levels.beginner: An environment is a separate workspace inside Power Platform. You might have one for testing and another for the real thing, so experiments never disturb live work.
levels.maker: An environment is a space to store, manage and share your organisation's business data, apps, agents and flows. Many organisations create separate ones for development, test and production, or for different teams or regions. You move things between environments with [[solution|solutions]].
levels.architect: Each environment is created under a Microsoft Entra tenant and is tied to a geography. It is where [[dataverse]] data, apps and flows live. Admins control creation, access and policy through the [[power-platform-admin-center]] and [[data-policy|data policies]]. Plan the environment strategy early, because it drives lifecycle management, access and cost.

terms.summary: An environment is a separate workspace inside Power Platform. You might have one for testing and another for the real thing, so experiments never disturb live work.

levels.beginner: Evaluation is testing an AI helper to see whether its answers are good enough.
levels.maker: Builders prepare sample questions and check things such as accuracy, safety, usefulness, speed and whether the task was completed, before and after changes.
levels.architect: Use a fixed set of test cases with clear criteria such as correctness, completeness and groundedness. Re-run them whenever instructions, knowledge or the model changes. Contrast with [[red-teaming]], which probes for weaknesses.

terms.summary: Evaluation is testing an AI helper to see whether its answers are good enough.

levels.beginner: Microsoft splits Copilot into two kinds of work: everyday AI, which your licence already pays for, and advanced AI, which you pay for as you use it.
levels.maker: Everyday AI is covered by the user licence. Advanced AI means long-running agentic work, such as [[cowork]], Code, [[autopilot]] and frontier models, and it runs on usage-based billing in [[copilot-credits]]. Knowing which side a feature falls on explains why a licensed user can still see extra charges.
levels.architect: Plan budgets by workload, not only by seat: licences cover the everyday side, while credit consumption scales with how much advanced work is run. Monitor consumption and set limits, because the boundary between the two can change as products evolve.

terms.summary: Microsoft splits Copilot into two kinds of work: everyday AI, which your licence already pays for, and advanced AI, which you pay for as you use it.

levels.beginner: An excluded item is something the search robot has been told to skip.
levels.maker: It is an item that is excluded from a crawl by the administrator of the host site or the search administrator of the crawler. It does not appear in search results because it was never gathered.
levels.architect: The exclusion is set by the administrator of the host site or by the search administrator. Check exclusions first if an item never appears in search.

terms.summary: An excluded item is something the search robot has been told to skip.

levels.beginner: Explainable AI makes it easier to understand why an AI gave a particular answer.
levels.maker: It helps people trust, question and challenge outputs.
levels.architect: Techniques include showing sources, reasoning summaries and feature attributions.

terms.summary: Explainable AI makes it easier to understand why an AI gave a particular answer.

levels.beginner: Extensibility is the ability to add new abilities to Copilot, like adding attachments to a toolbox.
levels.maker: You can extend Copilot with agents, data sources, connectors, actions and your own business logic.
levels.architect: Options include [[declarative-agent|declarative agents]], [[custom-engine-agent|custom engine agents]], APIs and [[model-context-protocol|MCP]] servers. Choose based on how much control you need over orchestration and hosting.

terms.summary: Extensibility is the ability to add new abilities to Copilot, like adding attachments to a toolbox.

levels.beginner: External data is information kept outside Microsoft 365 that you may allow an AI helper to use.
levels.maker: It might sit in another application or database. Approved integrations let Copilot use it, usually with the same access rules.
levels.architect: Bring it in with a [[graph-connector]], [[connector]] or MCP. Check that the source's permissions are respected and that how sensitive the data is is understood.

terms.summary: External data is information kept outside Microsoft 365 that you may allow an AI helper to use.

levels.beginner: An extracted definition is a sentence that the search system spotted and recognised as explaining a word.
levels.maker: It is the definition obtained by an index server during a crawl, to identify whether any sentences in the item match the pattern for defining a term. It applies to an [[extracted-term]].
levels.architect: The index server finds these during the crawl by matching sentences against a defining pattern. The result is linked to an [[extracted-term]].

terms.summary: An extracted definition is a sentence that the search system spotted and recognised as explaining a word.

levels.beginner: An extracted term is a word or phrase that search has picked out and has an explanation for.
levels.maker: It is a term that an [[extracted-definition]] applies to. Search can then show the definition next to the term.
levels.architect: The term is paired with the [[extracted-definition]] found during the crawl.

terms.summary: An extracted term is a word or phrase that search has picked out and has an explanation for.

levels.beginner: Fabric IQ is a Microsoft layer that helps AI make sense of an organisation's analytical data.
levels.maker: It is associated with Microsoft Fabric and helps agents work with governed data and analytical context, rather than raw tables.
levels.architect: It is one of the "IQ" layers alongside [[work-iq]]. Details are evolving, so confirm what it provides in current documentation.

terms.summary: Fabric IQ is a Microsoft layer that helps AI make sense of an organisation's analytical data.

levels.beginner: The Farm Administrators group is the group of people trusted to look after all the servers that run SharePoint.
levels.maker: It is a group of users that has permission to manage all the servers in a server farm. Members can run command-line operations and all the administrative tasks in [[central-administration-site|Central Administration]] for the server or server farm.
levels.architect: Membership grants farm-wide control, so keep it small. It is different from site-level groups, see [[sharepoint-groups]].

terms.summary: The Farm Administrators group is the group of people trusted to look after all the servers that run SharePoint.

levels.beginner: A farm solution is an old-style package of custom code that an administrator installs on the servers that run SharePoint, so it affects every site on those servers.
levels.maker: Farm solutions only exist on SharePoint Server, which is installed in an organisation's own datacentre. They are not supported in SharePoint Online. Modern customisations are built with the [[spfx]] instead.
levels.architect: A farm solution is a .wsp package deployed by a farm administrator and it runs full-trust server-side code inside the IIS worker process. A faulty solution can slow or destabilise the whole farm, which is why Microsoft steered customisation toward client-side models such as the [[spfx]].

terms.summary: A farm solution is an old-style package of custom code that an administrator installs on the servers that run SharePoint, so it affects every site on those servers.

levels.beginner: A feature definition is the instruction sheet for a feature, saying what it is called and what it can do.
levels.maker: It is an XML fragment that defines a feature and its attributes. The attributes include things such as its identifier and where it can be activated.
levels.architect: The definition is a fragment of XML. Its attributes identify the feature (see [[feature-identifier]]) and state its [[feature-scope]].

terms.summary: A feature definition is the instruction sheet for a feature, saying what it is called and what it can do.

levels.beginner: A feature identifier is the unique ID number for a feature, like a serial number.
levels.maker: It is a GUID that identifies a feature. Code and deployment files use it to refer to the feature.
levels.architect: The GUID is the stable way to reference a feature from code and configuration. It appears in the [[feature-definition]].

terms.summary: A feature identifier is the unique ID number for a feature, like a serial number.

levels.beginner: A feature property is a setting attached to a feature that has been switched on.
levels.maker: It is a property that is associated with an active feature at a particular scope. It lets a feature store small pieces of configuration.
levels.architect: The property is tied to an active feature at a given [[feature-scope]], so the same feature can carry different values at different scopes.

terms.summary: A feature property is a setting attached to a feature that has been switched on.

levels.beginner: The feature scope says how wide a feature reaches when it is turned on: one site, a whole group of sites, and so on.
levels.maker: It is the scope at which a feature can be activated. Choosing the scope decides where the feature's effect applies.
levels.architect: The scope is defined as part of the [[feature-definition]]. Pick the narrowest scope that does the job.

terms.summary: The feature scope says how wide a feature reaches when it is turned on: one site, a whole group of sites, and so on.

levels.beginner: A federated location is another place that can answer a search, so you can ask more than one library at once.
levels.maker: It is a source that returns a set of search results for a search query. The source can be a search service in the local farm or in another farm, or another search engine that complies with the OpenSearch protocol.
levels.architect: Sources can be local, remote or third party as long as they are OpenSearch-compliant. The [[federated-location-definition]] holds the settings.

terms.summary: A federated location is another place that can answer a search, so you can ask more than one library at once.

levels.beginner: A federated location definition is the instruction card that tells search how to ask another source and how to show its answers.
levels.maker: It holds the configuration settings that describe how to issue a query for a [[federated-location]] and how to display the search results.
levels.architect: The definition describes both the query to issue and the display of the results for a given [[federated-location]].

terms.summary: A federated location definition is the instruction card that tells search how to ask another source and how to show its answers.

levels.beginner: Feedback is you telling the AI whether an answer was good or bad.
levels.maker: A thumbs up or down, or a comment, helps builders and admins see where answers fall short and improve instructions.
levels.architect: Treat feedback as input to [[evaluation]]. Be aware that comments can contain sensitive information, so know where they are stored and who can read them.

terms.summary: Feedback is you telling the AI whether an answer was good or bad.

levels.beginner: A field internal name is the fixed behind-the-scenes name of a column, which stays the same even if the visible title changes.
levels.maker: It is a string that uniquely identifies a field in a content type or a [[sharepoint-list]]. Use it rather than the display name in formulas and code.
levels.architect: The internal name is set when the field is created and does not change when the display name is edited, so it is the safe key for code. See also [[site-column]].

terms.summary: A field internal name is the fixed behind-the-scenes name of a column, which stays the same even if the visible title changes.

levels.beginner: File grounding means giving the AI a file to base its answer on, like handing a colleague the document and asking about it.
levels.maker: You attach or point to a document and ask for a summary, an answer or a new document based on it. It keeps the AI to the material you chose.
levels.architect: The file becomes part of the [[context]] for that task. Permissions still apply, and large files may exceed the [[context-window]], so relevant parts are retrieved.

terms.summary: File grounding means giving the AI a file to base its answer on, like handing a colleague the document and asking about it.

levels.beginner: Finance Agents are AI assistants made for finance teams, to help with finance tasks.
levels.maker: They were called Copilot for Finance until April 2025. Like any [[agent]] they work within the access of the person using them. Check the current list of agents and what each one can do, because the line-up changes.
levels.architect: Access to finance data must follow your existing permissions, and any step that changes financial records needs the approvals you would require of a person. Validate outputs against source records before relying on them.

terms.summary: Finance Agents are AI assistants made for finance teams, to help with finance tasks.

levels.beginner: Fine-tuning is giving an AI model extra training so it gets better at a particular kind of task.
levels.maker: It is different from just giving the AI documents to read: it actually changes the model's behaviour. Many business needs are met by [[grounding]] instead, which is cheaper and easier to update.
levels.architect: It trains an existing [[ai-model]] further on curated examples. Consider data quality, cost, maintenance when the base model changes, and whether instructions plus retrieval would do the job.

terms.summary: Fine-tuning is giving an AI model extra training so it gets better at a particular kind of task.

levels.beginner: First-party agents are ready-made AI helpers that Microsoft supplies, so you hand them a job instead of building anything yourself.
levels.maker: They come bundled with the Microsoft 365 Copilot licence and include Researcher, Analyst, Facilitator, Interpreter and Project Manager, among others. You delegate work to them, which makes them the easiest way to start with agents before you build your own with [[agent-builder]] or [[copilot-studio]].
levels.architect: They are maintained by Microsoft, so you cannot change their internals, unlike a [[declarative-agent]] or [[custom-engine-agent]] you author. Like other Copilot features they work within the signed-in user's permissions, and the set on offer can change, so check current documentation.

terms.summary: First-party agents are ready-made AI helpers that Microsoft supplies, so you hand them a job instead of building anything yourself.

levels.beginner: A form is the screen where people create, read or update one row, like a paper form with a box for each detail.
levels.maker: Every table has at least one main form. There are four types of form: main, quick create, quick view and card. You design forms in the form designer, arranging tabs, sections and controls.
levels.architect: Forms are metadata bound to a [[dataverse-table]], made of tabs, sections and controls. Form scripts run in the browser, so important rules belong in the data layer as well. Ship forms in a [[solution]].

terms.summary: A form is the screen where people create, read or update one row, like a paper form with a box for each detail.

levels.beginner: Forms Copilot is AI help for making surveys and forms.
levels.maker: Where available it can suggest questions and help refine a form so you can create one faster.
levels.architect: Review generated questions for bias and clarity, and check where responses are stored.

terms.summary: Forms Copilot is AI help for making surveys and forms.

levels.beginner: Freshness is how up to date the information given to an AI is.
levels.maker: If the AI uses old data, its answer may be out of date. Recent web or organisational data improves answers for fast-changing topics.
levels.architect: Freshness depends on index update times, caching and the source. Where decisions depend on recent facts, prefer live retrieval and show dates in [[citation|citations]].

terms.summary: Freshness is how up to date the information given to an AI is.

levels.beginner: Frontier is Microsoft's early-access club: an opt-in programme that lets your organisation try new Microsoft 365 features before they are officially released.
levels.maker: It covers both AI and non-AI features. An administrator enrols chosen users in the Microsoft 365 admin centre, under Copilot, then Settings, then Copilot Frontier. Everything in it is a [[preview]], so features can change and may behave differently from finished ones.
levels.architect: Frontier experiences are previews with their own terms. For example, they are not covered by the HIPAA business associate agreement, so check compliance needs before enrolling users who handle regulated data. Treat the programme as a controlled way to test ahead of [[general-availability]], not as a production commitment.

terms.summary: Frontier is Microsoft's early-access club: an opt-in programme that lets your organisation try new Microsoft 365 features before they are officially released.

levels.beginner: The FSA Manager is the supervisor service that runs the security side of FAST search.
levels.maker: It is the Windows service that provides administration functionality for FAST Search Authorization (FSA). It works together with the [[fsa-worker]].
levels.architect: FSA filters search results to enforce document-level security. The manager provides administration, while the [[fsa-worker]] generates the [[user-search-security-filter|user search security filters]].

terms.summary: The FSA Manager is the supervisor service that runs the security side of FAST search.

levels.beginner: The FSA worker is the helper service that works out what each person is allowed to see in search.
levels.maker: It is the Windows service that generates user search security filters in FAST Search Authorization. Together with the [[fsa-manager]], it keeps search results secure.
levels.architect: The worker builds the [[user-search-security-filter|user search security filters]] that FSA uses to trim results.

terms.summary: The FSA worker is the helper service that works out what each person is allowed to see in search.

levels.beginner: A full-text index component is a set of files that works like the index at the back of a book, listing where each word is found.
levels.maker: It is a set of files that contains all the index keys extracted from a set of items. Search uses it to find items quickly.
levels.architect: The component stores the index keys extracted from items. It is one piece of the [[search-catalog]] machinery that supports queries.

terms.summary: A full-text index component is a set of files that works like the index at the back of a book, listing where each word is found.

levels.beginner: General availability, or GA, means a feature is officially ready for everyone to use.
levels.maker: It is the release stage after [[preview]]. GA features are covered by Microsoft's published service terms for broad production use.
levels.architect: Check each feature's stage before depending on it. Support, SLAs and change notice differ from [[preview]] features.

terms.summary: General availability, or GA, means a feature is officially ready for everyone to use.

levels.beginner: Generation is the AI writing its answer, one small piece at a time.
levels.maker: You see the answer appear gradually because the model produces it piece by piece based on your request and the context.
levels.architect: The model predicts the next [[token]] repeatedly until it stops. It is the output part of [[inference]].

terms.summary: Generation is the AI writing its answer, one small piece at a time.

levels.beginner: Generative AI is AI that creates new things, such as text, images or code, from your instructions.
levels.maker: It is what sits behind Copilot's writing and summarising. It makes new content rather than just sorting or labelling existing content.
levels.architect: Models generate output probabilistically from learned patterns, which explains both their fluency and the risk of [[hallucination]]. See also [[non-deterministic-output]].

terms.summary: Generative AI is AI that creates new things, such as text, images or code, from your instructions.

levels.beginner: A generative answer is a reply the AI composes on the spot, rather than picking a pre-written one.
levels.maker: In an agent, it lets the agent answer from its knowledge sources even where you haven't scripted a topic for that question.
levels.architect: It is produced by a model using retrieved [[knowledge-source|knowledge]]. Fixed [[topic|topics]] give predictability; generative answers give breadth. Many agents combine both.

terms.summary: A generative answer is a reply the AI composes on the spot, rather than picking a pre-written one.

levels.beginner: A generic list is the plain, all-purpose kind of list: a simple table that you shape yourself.
levels.maker: It is a [[sharepoint-list]] whose base type is Generic List. Most custom lists you create from scratch are of this kind.
levels.architect: The base type is Generic List, which is the basis for many list types. Other base types exist, for example for document libraries.

terms.summary: A generic list is the plain, all-purpose kind of list: a simple table that you shape yourself.

levels.beginner: Governance is the set of rules and responsibilities that decide how Copilot and agents may be created and used.
levels.maker: It covers who can build agents, what data they can reach, how they are monitored and what happens when something goes wrong.
levels.architect: Combine [[policy|policies]], [[lifecycle-management]], monitoring and ownership. Start early, because agents can spread quickly once users can create them.

terms.summary: Governance is the set of rules and responsibilities that decide how Copilot and agents may be created and used.

levels.beginner: GPT is a family of AI language models, and the name stands for generative pre-trained transformer.
levels.maker: Microsoft Copilot experiences may use OpenAI models like these alongside Microsoft's own services and controls.
levels.architect: GPT is a model family, not a product. What a user experiences also depends on [[orchestration]], grounding and safety layers.

terms.summary: GPT is a family of AI language models, and the name stands for generative pre-trained transformer.

levels.beginner: A Graph connector brings content from another system into Microsoft's search and AI, so people can find it in one place.
levels.maker: Use it to make information outside Microsoft 365 searchable and usable by Copilot while keeping the configured access rules.
levels.architect: It indexes external items into the Microsoft Graph-based search index with access control lists. Map permissions carefully, so that [[permission-trimming]] works as intended.

terms.summary: A Graph connector brings content from another system into Microsoft's search and AI, so people can find it in one place.

levels.beginner: Graph grounding means the AI uses your work information, like files, mail and meetings, to answer you.
levels.maker: It makes answers specific to your work. It only uses what you already have access to.
levels.architect: Retrieval runs over [[microsoft-graph]] content and honours the user's permissions through [[permission-trimming]].

terms.summary: Graph grounding means the AI uses your work information, like files, mail and meetings, to answer you.

levels.beginner: A grounded response is an answer that was based on real sources, not just the AI's memory.
levels.maker: It is more likely to be accurate and specific, and often comes with [[citation|citations]].
levels.architect: It is the result of [[grounding]]. It lowers, but does not eliminate, the risk of [[hallucination]].

terms.summary: A grounded response is an answer that was based on real sources, not just the AI's memory.

levels.beginner: Grounding means giving the AI the right facts to answer from, such as your documents, so it does not have to guess.
levels.maker: [[microsoft-365-copilot]] grounds answers in the work data a person can access, and an [[agent]] is grounded through its [[knowledge-source|knowledge sources]]. Grounded answers are easier to check because you can see where they came from.
levels.architect: Grounding usually retrieves relevant passages at request time and adds them to the prompt, which is known as retrieval-augmented generation. Quality depends on search quality, permission trimming and content freshness. It reduces, but does not remove, [[hallucination]].

terms.summary: Grounding means giving the AI the right facts to answer from, such as your documents, so it does not have to guess.

levels.beginner: It is the unique reference number for a document that is going through a group sign-off.
levels.maker: It is a string that uniquely identifies a document that is subject to the policies defined for a Group Approval workflow. A protocol server generates and assigns it automatically.
levels.architect: The string is generated and assigned to the document by a protocol server, not by the author. Use it to refer to the document in the approval process, and do not confuse it with the [[workflow-identifier]].

terms.summary: It is the unique reference number for a document that is going through a group sign-off.

levels.beginner: A guardrail is a safety rail that keeps an AI from going where it should not.
levels.maker: It can be a filter, a rule or a limit that stops unsafe, inappropriate or out-of-scope behaviour.
levels.architect: Guardrails can be technical (filters, allow-lists, [[permission-trimming]]) or procedural ([[policy|policies]], approvals). Layer them, because none is sufficient on its own.

terms.summary: A guardrail is a safety rail that keeps an AI from going where it should not.

levels.beginner: A hallucination is when an AI states something that sounds confident but is wrong or made up.
levels.maker: It happens because a [[large-language-model]] predicts likely wording rather than looking facts up. [[grounding|Grounding]] in trusted content, asking for sources and checking important answers all help.
levels.architect: Hallucinations include invented facts, citations and numbers. Mitigate them with grounding, tightly scoped instructions, evaluation sets that include questions with no answer, and human review for decisions that matter. Do not assume any mitigation removes them completely.

terms.summary: A hallucination is when an AI states something that sounds confident but is wrong or made up.

levels.beginner: Hallucination mitigation is the set of tricks used to stop an AI from making things up.
levels.maker: Giving the AI real sources, asking for citations, testing and human review all lower the chance of an invented answer.
levels.architect: Combine [[grounding]], [[citation|citations]], [[evaluation]] and [[human-in-the-loop]] review. Reduction is realistic; elimination is not.

terms.summary: Hallucination mitigation is the set of tricks used to stop an AI from making things up.

levels.beginner: A handoff is when a job passes from one agent or step to another, or to a real person.
levels.maker: In support scenarios an agent may pass the case to a human when it can't help. The next owner needs enough context to continue.
levels.architect: Design what context is passed, what happens if no one is available, and how the user is told. Include the conversation summary so people don't have to repeat themselves.

terms.summary: A handoff is when a job passes from one agent or step to another, or to a real person.

levels.beginner: Harmful content is material that could be unsafe, abusive, hateful or otherwise inappropriate.
levels.maker: AI services use safety controls and moderation to detect and limit it in what people ask and what the AI replies.
levels.architect: Controls apply to both inputs and outputs. Configure thresholds and review settings for your use case rather than assuming defaults suit it.

terms.summary: Harmful content is material that could be unsafe, abusive, hateful or otherwise inappropriate.

levels.beginner: A harness is the engine underneath an agent in Copilot Studio. The builder looks the same, but the engine decides how the agent behaves.
levels.maker: It sets how independently the agent reasons, which files it can touch, where you can publish it and, importantly, how it is billed and whether your existing licences cover it. Today there are three: the [[microsoft-copilot-harness]], the [[standard-harness]] and the [[customer-conversation-harness]].
levels.architect: Choose the harness first, because it fixes the cost model and the publishing options, and an agent cannot be moved to a different harness after it is created. Do not confuse it with the [[orchestrator]], which is the component that coordinates steps inside an agent. The set of harnesses is evolving, so check the current harness overview.

terms.summary: A harness is the engine underneath an agent in Copilot Studio. The builder looks the same, but the engine decides how the agent behaves.

levels.beginner: A high confidence property is a piece of information that is a very strong clue that an item is exactly what someone is looking for.
levels.maker: It is a managed property from the [[metadata-index]] that the administrator identifies as a good indicator of a highly relevant item. It is used to produce a [[high-confidence-result]].
levels.architect: Administrators pick the properties that count. A precise match between a property value and the tokens in the query text then produces a [[high-confidence-result]].

terms.summary: A high confidence property is a piece of information that is a very strong clue that an item is exactly what someone is looking for.

levels.beginner: A high confidence result is a search answer that search is very sure about, shown prominently.
levels.maker: It is a search result that is considered highly relevant because of a precise match between a [[high-confidence-property]] value and the tokens in the query text.
levels.architect: The result comes from matching query tokens exactly against the value of a [[high-confidence-property]].

terms.summary: A high confidence result is a search answer that search is very sure about, shown prominently.

levels.beginner: A high-trust app is an add-in that is trusted to say for itself who the user is.
levels.maker: It is an app that uses the [[server-to-server-protocol]]. The app is responsible for creating the user portion of the access token, so it is trusted to assert any user identity. This applies to [[sharepoint-add-in|SharePoint Add-ins]].
levels.architect: Because the app builds the user part of the access token itself, it can claim any user identity, so trust must be granted with care. The add-in model is retired in SharePoint Online, so this is relevant for SharePoint Server.

terms.summary: A high-trust app is an add-in that is trusted to say for itself who the user is.

levels.beginner: The home site is the one SharePoint site that acts as your organisation's front door, the landing page for the company intranet. It is the site people reach first from the SharePoint start page and from Viva Connections.
levels.maker: An organisation has at most one home site, and an admin chooses it. It has to be a [[communication-site]], and it is normally also set up as a [[hub-site]] so that news and navigation can flow to the other sites. It is the entry point of the intranet, not just another hub.
levels.architect: Set at tenant level by an administrator, for example with the Set-SPOHomeSite cmdlet. One home site exists per tenant and it must be a modern communication site. It drives the Home experience in SharePoint and Viva Connections, so plan its navigation and audience targeting with the whole organisation in mind.

terms.summary: The home site is the one SharePoint site that acts as your organisation's front door, the landing page for the company intranet. It is the site people reach first from the SharePoint start page and from Viva Connections.

levels.beginner: The host web is the ordinary SharePoint site that an add-in is installed on. It is the place where the add-in's features show up.
levels.maker: When you install a [[sharepoint-add-in]], it attaches to a host web. The add-in's own files live in a separate [[app-web]]. The add-in asks for permission to the host web when it is installed, and the site owner must agree to it.
levels.architect: Add-in code reaches the host web with cross-domain calls that are given the SPHostUrl and SPAppWebUrl values. The permissions the add-in may use on the host web are declared in its manifest as app permission requests. Do not confuse it with the [[app-web]], which belongs to the add-in.

terms.summary: The host web is the ordinary SharePoint site that an add-in is installed on. It is the place where the add-in's features show up.

levels.beginner: A hub site links related SharePoint sites together so they feel like one connected area. Picture a department lobby with doors to several rooms: every room shares the same signs and style, and the news from all of them shows up in the lobby.
levels.maker: A SharePoint admin registers a team or communication site as a hub, and other sites then join it. Joined sites share navigation and theme, and news and activity from them roll up on the hub. A site can belong to only one hub at a time. A hub is not the same as the [[home-site]], which is the single front door for the whole organisation.
levels.architect: Hub association is a flat relationship, not a hierarchy, and it replaces deep subsite structures. Joining a hub does not change permissions: visitors only see content from associated sites that they already have access to, because search results are security trimmed. Hubs are registered and managed with admin tools such as the SharePoint admin center or PowerShell.

terms.summary: A hub site links related SharePoint sites together so they feel like one connected area. Picture a department lobby with doors to several rooms: every room shares the same signs and style, and the news from all of them shows up in the lobby.

levels.beginner: Human-in-the-loop means a person checks or approves what the AI does before it counts.
levels.maker: This is sensible for important outputs and actions such as sending emails, changing records or spending money.
levels.architect: Put approvals where risk is high and make the review easy and informed. Rubber-stamping without context defeats the purpose.

terms.summary: Human-in-the-loop means a person checks or approves what the AI does before it counts.

levels.beginner: Hybrid search combines searching for exact words with searching by meaning.
levels.maker: This helps you find things even when you don't remember the exact wording, while still catching exact names and codes.
levels.architect: Results from [[keyword-search]] and [[vector-search]] are merged and ranked together. It tends to beat either method alone on varied queries.

terms.summary: Hybrid search combines searching for exact words with searching by meaning.

levels.beginner: Identity is the verified "who" behind an action, whether a person, a service or an agent.
levels.maker: Access, audit and permitted actions all depend on identity. If Copilot acts for you, it acts with your identity and rights.
levels.architect: Agents may run under the user's identity or their own. Choose deliberately, since it decides what the agent can reach and how actions are audited.

terms.summary: Identity is the verified "who" behind an action, whether a person, a service or an agent.

levels.beginner: Image generation is when AI draws a picture from a written description.
levels.maker: It can speed up mockups and illustrations. Check rights, brand fit and accuracy before using the results.
levels.architect: Policies on use, labelling and [[protected-material]] apply to generated images as to other [[ai-generated-content]].

terms.summary: Image generation is when AI draws a picture from a written description.

levels.beginner: Implicit context is the background an app supplies on its own, like the document you have open, without you attaching anything.
levels.maker: It saves effort, but it also means the AI may be using something you did not consciously select.
levels.architect: The application decides what is included. Understand what is sent so that sensitive content is not exposed unintentionally. See also [[app-context]].

terms.summary: Implicit context is the background an app supplies on its own, like the document you have open, without you attaching anything.

levels.beginner: Inference is the moment a trained AI actually answers a new request.
levels.maker: Training builds the model once. Inference is the day-to-day work of using it.
levels.architect: Inference cost and [[latency]] depend on model size and input length. Capacity limits and [[quota|quotas]] affect it.

terms.summary: Inference is the moment a trained AI actually answers a new request.

levels.beginner: An information barrier is a wall between two groups of people that stops them communicating or sharing.
levels.maker: Organisations use it to meet regulatory or conflict-of-interest rules, for example between departments.
levels.architect: It is a [[microsoft-purview]] control. Consider how barriers interact with Copilot's retrieval and with shared content.

terms.summary: An information barrier is a wall between two groups of people that stops them communicating or sharing.

levels.beginner: Input is whatever you give the AI: your question, files, pictures or data.
levels.maker: Besides your typed [[prompt]], inputs can include chat history, instructions and retrieved content.
levels.architect: Treat all input as potentially untrusted, because content retrieved into a request may carry instructions (see [[prompt-injection]]).

terms.summary: Input is whatever you give the AI: your question, files, pictures or data.

levels.beginner: Intent is what you are really trying to achieve, which the AI tries to work out from your words.
levels.maker: If you write "my laptop won't start", the intent might be "get IT support".
levels.architect: Agents use intent to route to a [[topic]] or [[agent-action]]. Ambiguous phrasing needs clarifying questions.

terms.summary: Intent is what you are really trying to achieve, which the AI tries to work out from your words.

levels.beginner: Isolation keeps things apart so a problem or a breach in one place can't spread to others.
levels.maker: Agents, environments and data can be separated so that an agent can't reach anything outside what it is meant to.
levels.architect: Use separate [[environment|environments]], identities and permissions. It is a core part of limiting blast radius.

terms.summary: Isolation keeps things apart so a problem or a breach in one place can't spread to others.

levels.beginner: A jailbreak is a trick that gets an AI to ignore its own safety rules.
levels.maker: People write clever prompts to push a model into producing things it is meant to refuse. Builders test for this before releasing an agent.
levels.architect: Jailbreaks target the model's own safety behaviour, whereas [[prompt-injection]] smuggles instructions in through content. Defend with layered [[guardrail|guardrails]], [[moderation]] and [[red-teaming]].

terms.summary: A jailbreak is a trick that gets an AI to ignore its own safety rules.

levels.beginner: Job automation is using AI and tools to take over the repeatable parts of someone's work.
levels.maker: The routine steps are handled automatically, while people keep the judgement calls and the accountability.
levels.architect: Decide which tasks are rule-based enough to automate and which need a person. Keep an owner for exceptions and a way to audit what ran.

terms.summary: Job automation is using AI and tools to take over the repeatable parts of someone's work.

levels.beginner: JSON is a simple, tidy text format for passing information between programs, a bit like a filled-in form.
levels.maker: You will see it when connecting agents and services: data is sent as named items in curly brackets.
levels.architect: Many agent features use JSON: [[tool-calling]] parameters, [[adaptive-card|Adaptive Cards]] and API responses. Validate it before trusting it, as models can produce malformed JSON.

terms.summary: JSON is a simple, tidy text format for passing information between programs, a bit like a filled-in form.

levels.beginner: Just-in-time access gives someone powerful rights only when they need them, and only for a short while.
levels.maker: It stops people holding standing admin rights that could be misused or stolen.
levels.architect: It is a form of privileged access management. Combine it with approval, time limits and logging. It supports [[least-privilege]].

terms.summary: Just-in-time access gives someone powerful rights only when they need them, and only for a short while.

levels.beginner: A key phrase is a short phrase that captures an important idea in some content.
levels.maker: Pulling out key phrases helps with search, sorting and summaries.
levels.architect: Key phrase extraction is a language technique, related to [[named-entity-recognition]], and is useful as a signal for classification and search.

terms.summary: A key phrase is a short phrase that captures an important idea in some content.

levels.beginner: A keyword consumer is a group of sites that all use the same set of search keywords and recommended answers.
levels.maker: It is a site collection that uses a particular set of keywords, synonyms and Best Bets. See [[keyword-synonym]].
levels.architect: The consumer is a [[site-collection]] that shares one set of keywords, synonyms and Best Bets.

terms.summary: A keyword consumer is a group of sites that all use the same set of search keywords and recommended answers.

levels.beginner: Keyword search finds things by matching the exact words you type.
levels.maker: It is quick and exact, but it won't find a document that uses different wording for the same idea.
levels.architect: Modern systems combine it with [[semantic-search]] in [[hybrid-search]]. Keyword matching remains the best way to find codes, names and exact phrases.

terms.summary: Keyword search finds things by matching the exact words you type.

levels.beginner: A keyword synonym is another way of saying the same search word, such as "car" for "automobile".
levels.maker: It is an alternate phrasing of a particular keyword. When a user types a synonym, search returns the same Best Bet result as for the keyword.
levels.architect: Synonyms map extra phrasings to a keyword so that they return the same Best Bet. They belong to a set used by a [[keyword-consumer]].

terms.summary: A keyword synonym is another way of saying the same search word, such as "car" for "automobile".

levels.beginner: A knowledge graph is a map of things and how they relate, such as people, projects and documents.
levels.maker: It helps a system understand that a person works on a project that has certain files.
levels.architect: It stores entities and relationships. Despite the similar name, [[microsoft-graph]] is an API and data layer for Microsoft 365, not a generic knowledge graph.

terms.summary: A knowledge graph is a map of things and how they relate, such as people, projects and documents.

levels.beginner: Knowledge is what an agent is allowed to read in order to answer you, such as a set of documents, a website or a database.
levels.maker: You tailor an [[agent]]'s answers by giving it specialised instructions and data sources. Good knowledge is accurate, current and open to the people asking: an agent only answers well from content its users are allowed to see.
levels.architect: Knowledge can come from Microsoft 365 content such as SharePoint sites and libraries, from external systems through connectors, or from other sources the platform supports. Retrieval quality, permissions and freshness matter as much as the model, so test with real questions and review who can read the source content. See also [[grounding]].

terms.summary: Knowledge is what an agent is allowed to read in order to answer you, such as a set of documents, a website or a database.

levels.beginner: KQL is an abbreviation for two different query languages, so check which one is meant.
levels.maker: Kusto Query Language is used to analyse large sets of logs and telemetry. Keyword Query Language is used in Microsoft search scenarios.
levels.architect: The context decides the meaning: Kusto for analysing telemetry, Keyword Query Language for search. The two are unrelated in syntax.

terms.summary: KQL is an abbreviation for two different query languages, so check which one is meant.

levels.beginner: Language auto-detection means the system works out for itself which language a document is written in.
levels.maker: It is a process that automatically determines the language code identifier (LCID) for the text in a document. It saves people from labelling every file.
levels.architect: The result is an LCID, the language code identifier for the text of the document. Detection is automatic, so check the result for short or mixed-language text.

terms.summary: Language auto-detection means the system works out for itself which language a document is written in.

levels.beginner: A large language model, or LLM, is a computer program trained on huge amounts of text so it can predict and write language. That is what lets AI assistants hold a conversation.
levels.maker: LLMs power the chat and writing features in [[microsoft-365-copilot]] and [[copilot-studio]]. They write fluent text, but they do not know your business unless you [[grounding|ground]] them in your own content, and they can produce confident mistakes (a [[hallucination]]).
levels.architect: A model is fixed after training and works within a limited context window, so applications retrieve relevant content at request time and pass it in with the [[prompt]]. The choice of model affects quality, speed and cost. In a [[declarative-agent]] the platform chooses it, and in a [[custom-engine-agent]] you do.

terms.summary: A large language model, or LLM, is a computer program trained on huge amounts of text so it can predict and write language. That is what lets AI assistants hold a conversation.

levels.beginner: Latency is how long you wait between asking and getting the answer.
levels.maker: Bigger tasks, long prompts and complex agents take longer.
levels.architect: Latency is affected by model size, [[context-window]] use, [[tool-calling|tool calls]] and retrieval. Measure it as part of [[evaluation]].

terms.summary: Latency is how long you wait between asking and getting the answer.

levels.beginner: Least privilege means giving a person or app only the rights needed to do its job, and nothing extra.
levels.maker: Narrow rights limit what can go wrong. This matters more for agents that can act on your behalf.
levels.architect: Apply it to users, apps and agent identities. Review permissions regularly and combine it with [[role-based-access-control]].

terms.summary: Least privilege means giving a person or app only the rights needed to do its job, and nothing extra.

levels.beginner: A licence is what you pay for or are assigned that unlocks a feature for you.
levels.maker: Which Copilot features, agents and admin tools you get depends on your licence, and some use is billed by consumption instead.
levels.architect: Licensing and usage allowances change often, so check current Microsoft documentation. See also [[usage-based-billing]].

terms.summary: A licence is what you pay for or are assigned that unlocks a feature for you.

levels.beginner: Lifecycle management is looking after an agent from the first idea until it is switched off.
levels.maker: That means building, testing, approving, releasing, monitoring, updating and retiring it, in a controlled way.
levels.architect: Define owners, review points and retirement criteria. Orphaned agents are a common governance gap.

terms.summary: Lifecycle management is looking after an agent from the first idea until it is switched off.

levels.beginner: Line-of-business data is the information kept in a company's main operational systems, such as sales, finance or support.
levels.maker: It is often the most valuable data for an agent, and the most sensitive.
levels.architect: It is usually reached through [[connector|connectors]], APIs or [[model-context-protocol|MCP]]. Mirror the source system's permissions.

terms.summary: Line-of-business data is the information kept in a company's main operational systems, such as sales, finance or support.

levels.beginner: A list folder is a folder inside a list that keeps related items together.
levels.maker: It is a folder contained within a [[sharepoint-list]]. It can contain documents or list items, and it keeps the characteristics of the other items in the list, such as the schema that can be customised.
levels.architect: Folder items share the schema of the list. See [[parent-list]] for the list that contains an item or folder.

terms.summary: A list folder is a folder inside a list that keeps related items together.

levels.beginner: A list form is the page where you fill in or look at the details of one list item.
levels.maker: It is a page that lets users create, view or edit an item in a [[sharepoint-list]]. The page that creates a new item is the [[new-form]].
levels.architect: The form is shown through the [[list-form-web-part]]. Different forms exist for creating, viewing and editing.

terms.summary: A list form is the page where you fill in or look at the details of one list item.

levels.beginner: The List Form web part is the building block that draws a list form on a page.
levels.maker: It is a [[web-part]] used to display, edit or view an item in a list. It is what you see on a [[list-form]].
levels.architect: The part renders the item for display, editing or viewing inside a [[list-form]].

terms.summary: The List Form web part is the building block that draws a list form on a page.

levels.beginner: A list identifier is the unique code of a list, so that it can never be confused with another list.
levels.maker: It is a GUID used to identify a [[sharepoint-list]] in a [[site-collection]]. Use it when you have to point at one list exactly.
levels.architect: The GUID identifies the list within a site collection, unlike the [[list-item-identifier]], which identifies an item in the list.

terms.summary: A list identifier is the unique code of a list, so that it can never be confused with another list.

levels.beginner: A list item attachment is a file stuck onto a list item, like a document paper-clipped to a form.
levels.maker: It is a file contained within a list item. It is stored in a folder in the list with the segment "Attachments" in its path.
levels.architect: The files are stored in a folder in the list. The path of the folder contains the segment "Attachments".

terms.summary: A list item attachment is a file stuck onto a list item, like a document paper-clipped to a form.

levels.beginner: A list item identifier is the number that picks out one item in a list.
levels.maker: It is an integer that uniquely identifies an item in a [[sharepoint-list]]. It is also referred to as the item identifier.
levels.architect: Unlike the GUID-based [[list-identifier]], this is an integer that is unique within the list. Combine the two to point at a specific item.

terms.summary: A list item identifier is the number that picks out one item in a list.

levels.beginner: A list server template value tells SharePoint which kind of list blueprint was used.
levels.maker: It is a value that identifies the template used for a list. It is not the same as a saved [[list-template]] file.
levels.architect: The value identifies the template of the list. See [[list-template-identifier]] for the GUID used to identify a list template.

terms.summary: A list server template value tells SharePoint which kind of list blueprint was used.

levels.beginner: A list template is a saved pattern for a list, so you can create more lists exactly like it.
levels.maker: It is an XML-based definition of list settings, including fields and views, and optionally list items. List templates are stored in .stp files in the content database.
levels.architect: The definition is XML-based and stored as .stp files in the content database. The template is identified with a [[list-template-identifier]].

terms.summary: A list template is a saved pattern for a list, so you can create more lists exactly like it.

levels.beginner: A list template identifier is the unique code of a list template.
levels.maker: It is a GUID used to identify a [[list-template]]. Do not mix it up with the value used by a [[list-server-template]].
levels.architect: Use the GUID to point at one template exactly. It identifies the [[list-template]], not the list.

terms.summary: A list template identifier is the unique code of a list template.

levels.beginner: A list view page is a page whose main job is to show a list.
levels.maker: It is a web part page that displays a view of a list. It uses the [[list-view-web-part]] to show the items.
levels.architect: The page is a web part page and the display is generated by a [[list-view-web-part]].

terms.summary: A list view page is a page whose main job is to show a list.

levels.beginner: The list view threshold is a safety limit that stops one view or search from working through too many items at once, so a big list does not slow everyone down.
levels.maker: The limit is 5,000 items, but it applies to how many items an operation has to look at, not to how many a list holds. A [[sharepoint-list]] or [[document-library]] can contain far more. To stay under the limit, add indexes to the columns you filter or sort by and design views that narrow the data first.
levels.architect: A query that needs a full scan of more than 5,000 items is blocked, while a query that filters on an indexed column first is allowed. Lists and libraries can hold up to 30 million items. Some operations, such as breaking permissions or deleting a very large folder, can also reach the limit. Use indexed filters, paging and batching in code. On [[sharepoint-server]] the farm administrator can change the thresholds, although staying within the defaults is wiser.

terms.summary: The list view threshold is a safety limit that stops one view or search from working through too many items at once, so a big list does not slow everyone down.

levels.beginner: The List View web part is the reusable block that shows a list's items as a table on a page.
levels.maker: It is a reusable component that generates HTML-based views of the items in a SharePoint list. It is related to the [[data-view-web-part]].
levels.architect: The part generates HTML for the items of a list and is a reusable component that is placed on pages such as a [[list-view-page]].

terms.summary: The List View web part is the reusable block that shows a list's items as a table on a page.

levels.beginner: A log is a written record of what happened, kept so someone can look back later.
levels.maker: Logs help with fixing problems, checking security and understanding use.
levels.architect: Decide what to log, for how long and who can read it. Logs may hold sensitive information. Compare [[trace|traces]] and the [[unified-audit-log]].

terms.summary: A log is a written record of what happened, kept so someone can look back later.

levels.beginner: A log level is a dial that sets how much detail gets written to a log.
levels.maker: It is the amount of information that is stored in a log file for a transaction. Levels are represented by numbers or by words, from the most to the least verbose.
levels.architect: Raising the level adds detail, which helps in troubleshooting but makes logs larger. Lowering it keeps the logs small.

terms.summary: A log level is a dial that sets how much detail gets written to a log.

levels.beginner: A Loop component is a small live block of content, such as a list or table, that stays in sync wherever it is shared.
levels.maker: Edit it in a chat and the same change appears in an email or document. It works well with AI-generated working content.
levels.architect: Components stay synchronised across apps and follow sharing permissions of where they are stored.

terms.summary: A Loop component is a small live block of content, such as a list or table, that stays in sync wherever it is shared.

levels.beginner: A managed keyword is a tag you can add to an item so that it is easy to find and group later.
levels.maker: It is a word or phrase that is added to a SharePoint item, either as a value in the Managed Keyword column or as a social tag. Keywords are shared, so people can reuse them.
levels.architect: The keyword is added as a value in the Managed Keyword column or as a social tag. See the [[term-store]] for the managed metadata store.

terms.summary: A managed keyword is a tag you can add to an item so that it is easy to find and group later.

levels.beginner: A meeting recap is a summary of a meeting: key points, decisions and who is doing what.
levels.maker: It saves you from re-reading everything or watching the recording. It can also summarise a chat or document.
levels.architect: Where available it relies on a [[transcript]] or recording, so it needs to be enabled and permitted.

terms.summary: A meeting recap is a summary of a meeting: key points, decisions and who is doing what.

levels.beginner: A member group is a group of people that the profile service tracks, not the same as the site group called Members.
levels.maker: It is a group of users that is specific to the User Profile service. Do not confuse it with the [[members-group]] of a site.
levels.architect: The group is defined for the user profile service and its [[member-group-source]] identifies where it came from.

terms.summary: A member group is a group of people that the profile service tracks, not the same as the site group called Members.

levels.beginner: The member group source says where a group of people comes from, such as a particular company directory.
levels.maker: It is a qualified domain name, such as domain.corp.microsoft.com, that identifies the source of a [[member-group]].
levels.architect: The value is a qualified domain name. It names the source of the [[member-group]].

terms.summary: The member group source says where a group of people comes from, such as a particular company directory.

levels.beginner: The Members group is the standard group for the people who do the day-to-day work on a site.
levels.maker: It is a default group of users on a SharePoint site. By default the Members group is assigned the Contribute permission level. See [[sharepoint-groups]].
levels.architect: The default permission level is Contribute. Compare with the [[visitors-group]], which is given Read by default.

terms.summary: The Members group is the standard group for the people who do the day-to-day work on a site.

levels.beginner: It is the unique ID for one record about a group membership.
levels.maker: It is a unique identifier for a member group record. Use it when you need to refer to exactly one such record.
levels.architect: The identifier names one record of a [[member-group]] in the user profile data.

terms.summary: It is the unique ID for one record about a group membership.

levels.beginner: Memory lets an AI remember useful things about you or your work between chats.
levels.maker: It can keep preferences or working context so you don't repeat yourself, where the feature is supported and allowed.
levels.architect: Check what is stored, where, for how long and how users or admins can view or delete it. It differs from [[conversation-history]], which belongs to a chat.

terms.summary: Memory lets an AI remember useful things about you or your work between chats.

levels.beginner: Metadata is the "label on the box": facts about a file like its author, date and type.
levels.maker: Good metadata makes content easier to find and to control, and AI search uses it.
levels.architect: Search and retrieval use metadata for filtering, ranking and security trimming. Consistent metadata improves results.

terms.summary: Metadata is the "label on the box": facts about a file like its author, date and type.

levels.beginner: The metadata index is a catalogue, stored on a database server, of the details that go with each item.
levels.maker: It is a data structure on a back-end database server that stores the properties associated with each item and the attributes of those properties.
levels.architect: The index holds properties and their attributes. A [[high-confidence-property]] is a managed property taken from this index.

terms.summary: The metadata index is a catalogue, stored on a database server, of the details that go with each item.

levels.beginner: A metadata schema is the rule sheet that says what facts are kept about an item.
levels.maker: It is a schema used to manage information about an item. It defines the kinds of details that can be recorded.
levels.architect: Use the schema as the definition of what metadata exists. See [[content-type-schema]] for the schema of a content type.

terms.summary: A metadata schema is the rule sheet that says what facts are kept about an item.

levels.beginner: Microsoft 365 Archiving lets an organisation move SharePoint sites that nobody uses any more to cheaper storage, while keeping their content so it can be brought back later.
levels.maker: Admins archive a whole [[sharepoint-site]], not single files. An archived site cannot be used until an admin reactivates it. It is for content you want to keep but rarely need, and it is not the same as [[microsoft-365-backup]], which protects against loss. It used to be called Syntex Archiving.
levels.architect: Archiving works at the site level and keeps the content in a lower-cost tier. Decide how it fits with retention policies and site lifecycle rules, and test how long reactivation takes before archiving sites that someone might need urgently. Check current limits and billing before you rely on it.

terms.summary: Microsoft 365 Archiving lets an organisation move SharePoint sites that nobody uses any more to cheaper storage, while keeping their content so it can be brought back later.

levels.beginner: Microsoft 365 Backup keeps backup copies of an organisation's SharePoint, OneDrive and Exchange content, so it can be put back quickly after it is lost or damaged.
levels.maker: Admins choose what to back up and can restore to an earlier point in time. It solves a different problem from the [[recycle-bin]], which only holds items someone deleted for a limited time, and from [[version-history]], which keeps earlier copies of a single file. It used to be called Syntex Backup.
levels.architect: Backup works at the service level, with restore points for whole sites or accounts rather than for single versions of files. Plan it next to retention policies, the recycle bin and versioning, because each protects against a different kind of loss. Check current availability, limits and billing before relying on it.

terms.summary: Microsoft 365 Backup keeps backup copies of an organisation's SharePoint, OneDrive and Exchange content, so it can be put back quickly after it is lost or damaged.

aliases: Microsoft Copilot with Enterprise Data Protection
Microsoft Copilot with Commercial Data Protection

renamed.to: Microsoft Copilot with Commercial Data Protection

renamed.from: Microsoft Copilot with Commercial Data Protection
renamed.to: Microsoft Copilot with Enterprise Data Protection

renamed.from: Microsoft Copilot with Enterprise Data Protection

levels.beginner: Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic) is the chat assistant for work: you type a question and get an answer, with your organisation's data protections in place.
levels.maker: It began as Bing Chat Enterprise and went through several names, including Microsoft Copilot with Enterprise Data Protection and Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat, before becoming Basic in April 2026. It is a chat experience. The fuller [[microsoft-365-copilot|Premium]] experience adds Copilot inside Microsoft 365 apps and deeper use of your work data, so check current plans for the exact split.
levels.architect: Because the name changed so often, logs and older admin articles may use any of the earlier names for the same experience. Data protection applies to prompts and responses, and administrators can control access and which [[agent|agents]] are available. Confirm current capabilities and licensing for each plan in your own tenant.

terms.summary: Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic) is the chat assistant for work: you type a question and get an answer, with your organisation's data protections in place.

levels.beginner: Microsoft 365 Copilot is an AI assistant built into Microsoft 365 apps such as Word, Outlook and Teams. You ask it in everyday language and it helps you write, summarise and find things, using your own work information.
levels.maker: It works across Microsoft 365 apps and Copilot Chat, using the work data you are allowed to see through [[microsoft-graph]]. Organisations extend it with [[agent|agents]]. Its name has changed several times, and in April 2026 it became Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium) next to [[microsoft-365-copilot-chat|Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic)]].
levels.architect: Copilot combines a [[large-language-model]] with your organisation's data, retrieved through [[microsoft-graph]] and limited to what each user is already allowed to see. Answers are only as good as the content and permissions behind them, so content that is shared too widely, for example through broad [[sharing-link|sharing links]], can surface in answers. Extensibility comes through [[declarative-agent|declarative agents]] and [[custom-engine-agent|custom engine agents]].

terms.summary: Microsoft 365 Copilot is an AI assistant built into Microsoft 365 apps such as Word, Outlook and Teams. You ask it in everyday language and it helps you write, summarise and find things, using your own work information.

levels.beginner: The Microsoft 365 Copilot app is the home screen for Microsoft 365 on the web and your devices, where you start work, find your files and open Copilot.
levels.maker: It was called the Microsoft 365 app until December 2024. It brings your recent files, apps and Copilot Chat into one place. Do not confuse it with [[microsoft-365-copilot]], which is the AI assistant rather than the app that hosts it.
levels.architect: It is the front door to Microsoft 365 experiences and one of the places where people meet [[agent|agents]] next to chat. Administrators decide which apps and agents appear, so treat it as part of rollout planning rather than as a separate product.

terms.summary: The Microsoft 365 Copilot app is the home screen for Microsoft 365 on the web and your devices, where you start work, find your files and open Copilot.

levels.beginner: AppSource is Microsoft's online marketplace for ready-made business apps and add-ons, including ones for SharePoint, from Microsoft and other companies.
levels.maker: Instead of building something yourself or asking developers to add it to your own [[app-catalog]], you can find and add apps from the marketplace. Administrators decide whether people may get apps this way. It was previously known as the Office Store.
levels.architect: Partners list offers in the commercial marketplace. Solutions built with the [[spfx]] can be offered through it. Review each listing's permissions and data handling before allowing it in your tenant, in the same way as for a solution you deploy yourself.

terms.summary: AppSource is Microsoft's online marketplace for ready-made business apps and add-ons, including ones for SharePoint, from Microsoft and other companies.

aliases: GitHub Copilot harness in Copilot Studio

levels.beginner: The Microsoft Copilot harness is the engine for agents that work through a goal on their own, step by step. It used to be called the GitHub Copilot harness, and the name changed on 28 October 2026.
levels.maker: You describe the agent in plain language and give it instructions, knowledge, tools, skills and memory, instead of drawing topics and branches as you do with the [[standard-harness]]. It reasons through a goal, retries when a tool call fails, works with Word, Excel, PowerPoint and PDF files, and uses skills and hooks. It bills [[copilot-credits]] for all usage, both while you create the agent and while it runs, and a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence never covers it. You pick the harness when you create an agent and cannot move the agent to another harness later. Some things the standard harness has are missing: the SharePoint, WhatsApp and Dynamics 365 Contact Center channels, custom entities, manual authentication and Azure AI Search knowledge, and computer use is only planned.
levels.architect: Microsoft describes it as a shared foundation for agentic reasoning, tool use and orchestration, built by GitHub's engineering team and now used across Microsoft products, including Copilot Studio and Copilot Code. It supports more than 20 frontier models and bring-your-own-key, and open standards such as MCP and agent skills. In Copilot Studio it is an authoring and orchestration framework, not the GitHub Copilot service: it shares technology and SDK components with GitHub Copilot, but customer data is not sent to or processed by the GitHub Copilot service, and the existing Copilot Studio privacy, security and data residency commitments apply. Hooks replace topic triggers and skills replace prompt tools. Microsoft says existing agents continue with no change to capabilities or billing, and the new name appears in products and documentation over the following weeks, so older pages still say GitHub Copilot harness. Budget for it as a consumption workload, apply least privilege, review the actions taken and watch spend.

terms.summary: The Microsoft Copilot harness is the engine for agents that work through a goal on their own, step by step. It used to be called the GitHub Copilot harness, and the name changed on 28 October 2026.

levels.beginner: Microsoft Entra ID is the service that knows who your people are and signs them in.
levels.maker: It handles sign-ins and access controls across Microsoft 365 and many connected apps, including Copilot. Admins manage users, groups and conditional access there.
