levels.architect: It issues the tokens that apps and agents use for [[authentication]]. Many older articles use the previous name, Azure Active Directory (Azure AD).

terms.summary: Microsoft Entra ID is the service that knows who your people are and signs them in.

levels.beginner: Microsoft Graph is the connection point to the information in your Microsoft 365 account, such as your files, mail, meetings and people. It is how apps ask for that information in a controlled way.
levels.maker: [[microsoft-365-copilot]] uses enterprise data from Microsoft Graph, which is why it can talk about your own documents and meetings. Developers use the same Graph APIs to build their own integrations.
levels.architect: Graph is a REST API with a common sign-in model through Microsoft Entra. Permissions are either delegated, acting as the signed-in user, or application-level. In [[spfx]] solutions and agents, request only the scopes you need.

terms.summary: Microsoft Graph is the connection point to the information in your Microsoft 365 account, such as your files, mail, meetings and people. It is how apps ask for that information in a controlled way.

levels.beginner: Microsoft IQ is Microsoft's overall approach to giving agents knowledge of your work, data and context.
levels.maker: It groups intelligence layers such as [[work-iq]] and [[fabric-iq]] that supply context to agents.
levels.architect: This is an evolving umbrella term; check current documentation for what is included.

terms.summary: Microsoft IQ is Microsoft's overall approach to giving agents knowledge of your work, data and context.

levels.beginner: Microsoft Purview is the set of tools for protecting data and meeting compliance rules.
levels.maker: It includes labels, data loss prevention, audit and eDiscovery, all of which matter when Copilot can reach lots of content.
levels.architect: Use [[sensitivity-label|sensitivity labels]], [[data-loss-prevention]], [[ediscovery]] and the [[unified-audit-log]] to govern AI use.

terms.summary: Microsoft Purview is the set of tools for protecting data and meeting compliance rules.

levels.beginner: Microsoft Scout is a name you will meet in two places: the original name of Autopilot, and the name of a desktop app that works across your files and apps.
levels.maker: Learn still uses Microsoft Scout for the desktop app, available on Windows and macOS through [[frontier]]. It works across your files, command line, browser and Microsoft 365. The persistent agent that used to share the name is now called [[autopilot]].
levels.architect: Check which meaning a document intends. The desktop app is a Frontier experience, so preview terms apply, while the renamed persistent agent is a separate product with its own billing. Do not assume features or licensing carry across.

terms.summary: Microsoft Scout is a name you will meet in two places: the original name of Autopilot, and the name of a desktop app that works across your files and apps.

levels.beginner: Microsoft Search is the search tool across Microsoft 365 for finding people, files, sites and messages.
levels.maker: It returns only what you are allowed to see, and it also feeds Copilot.
levels.architect: Results are security-trimmed against the user's identity. See [[organisational-search]] and [[semantic-index]].

terms.summary: Microsoft Search is the search tool across Microsoft 365 for finding people, files, sites and messages.

levels.beginner: MCP is a common plug standard that lets AI tools connect to other tools and data in the same way.
levels.maker: Instead of building a custom link for each system, a system offers an MCP server and any compatible agent can use it.
levels.architect: It is an open protocol for discovering and using tools, resources and context. Treat each server as a trust boundary: review what it exposes, authenticate calls and log use.

terms.summary: MCP is a common plug standard that lets AI tools connect to other tools and data in the same way.

levels.beginner: A model-driven app is built around your data: you decide what information you keep and the app builds the screens for it. It is like starting from a filing system rather than a blank page.
levels.maker: You choose tables, forms, views and dashboards and describe how people move between them in a [[model-driven-site-map|site map]]. It needs [[dataverse]], and it adapts to phone, tablet and desktop. Choose it when the data and its rules matter more than a custom look; choose a [[canvas-app]] for a bespoke layout.
levels.architect: An app is a set of components, such as tables, forms, views, dashboards and pages, defined in the app designer and delivered through the Unified Interface. Behaviour comes from the data model: [[dataverse-column|columns]], relationships, business rules, [[business-process-flow|business process flows]] and [[security-role|security roles]]. Ship it in a [[solution]].

terms.summary: A model-driven app is built around your data: you decide what information you keep and the app builds the screens for it. It is like starting from a filing system rather than a blank page.

levels.beginner: A moderated object is something that must be checked by a reviewer before others can see it.
levels.maker: It is an object for which a moderator approves or rejects additions or changes. New objects and changes become visible to other users only after approval. See [[moderation-status]].
levels.architect: Visibility depends on approval. The state is tracked as the [[moderation-status]].

terms.summary: A moderated object is something that must be checked by a reviewer before others can see it.

levels.beginner: Moderation is checking what goes into and comes out of an AI so unsafe content is caught.
levels.maker: Automatic filters and human review help stop policy-breaking material.
levels.architect: Tune thresholds for your audience and review samples regularly.

terms.summary: Moderation is checking what goes into and comes out of an AI so unsafe content is caught.

levels.beginner: Moderation status is the label that says whether an item has been approved yet.
levels.maker: It is the content approval status of an item in a list. It matters for any [[moderated-object]].
levels.architect: The status of an item records where it stands in the approval process for a [[moderated-object]].

terms.summary: Moderation status is the label that says whether an item has been approved yet.

levels.beginner: Multimodal AI can handle more than one kind of information, such as text, pictures and sound.
levels.maker: You can show it a chart and ask a question about it.
levels.architect: Inputs and outputs may be in different forms, so test each. Policies on content apply to every type.

terms.summary: Multimodal AI can handle more than one kind of information, such as text, pictures and sound.

levels.beginner: A multivalue property is a field that can hold more than one value, like a contact with several phone numbers.
levels.maker: It is a property that can contain multiple values of the same variant type. Use it when one item needs several values of the same kind.
levels.architect: All values share one variant type. Code that reads the property must handle a list rather than a single value.

terms.summary: A multivalue property is a field that can hold more than one value, like a contact with several phone numbers.

levels.beginner: Named entity recognition finds the names of people, places, companies, dates and products in text.
levels.maker: It helps tag documents and extract facts.
levels.architect: A natural-language technique that labels spans of text with entity types. It is often a pre-processing step for search and classification.

terms.summary: Named entity recognition finds the names of people, places, companies, dates and products in text.

levels.beginner: Natural language is ordinary human language, the way you talk or write.
levels.maker: With Copilot you ask in everyday words instead of learning special commands.
levels.architect: Prompts in natural language are ambiguous, so clear context and constraints improve results.

terms.summary: Natural language is ordinary human language, the way you talk or write.

levels.beginner: Natural language processing is the field of teaching computers to understand and produce human language.
levels.maker: It underlies search, translation, summaries and chat.
levels.architect: Classical NLP tasks such as [[named-entity-recognition]] are now often handled by [[large-language-model|LLMs]].

terms.summary: Natural language processing is the field of teaching computers to understand and produce human language.

levels.beginner: A navigation structure is the signposting of a site: the links that lead you between its parts.
levels.maker: It is a hierarchical organisation of links between related content, such as lists within a site. It is what menus and quick-launch links are built from.
levels.architect: The structure is hierarchical, so links can be grouped under parents. Design it around how people look for things, not around how the site is built.

terms.summary: A navigation structure is the signposting of a site: the links that lead you between its parts.

levels.beginner: A neural network is a computer structure loosely inspired by the brain that learns patterns from examples.
levels.maker: It is the building block behind most modern AI models.
levels.architect: A network of layers with weights tuned during training. Large language models are very large neural networks.

terms.summary: A neural network is a computer structure loosely inspired by the brain that learns patterns from examples.

levels.beginner: A new form is the page you fill in to add a new item to a list.
levels.maker: It is a form that allows for the creation of a list item. It is one of the [[list-form|list forms]].
levels.architect: It is the creation counterpart of the view and edit forms; all of them are [[list-form|list forms]].

terms.summary: A new form is the page you fill in to add a new item to a list.

levels.beginner: A news post is a page that shares an announcement or a story with the people who follow a site. It appears in news feeds and on the SharePoint start page.
levels.maker: You create a news post from a site's home page or from the plus menu, write it like any [[site-page]], and publish it. The News web part collects posts and shows them on other pages, and posts can reach the intranet through a [[hub-site]] or the [[home-site]].
levels.architect: A news post is a site page whose promoted state marks it as news, which is what the News web part and the roll-up queries look for. Because it is still a page in the Site Pages library, it follows the same permissions and publishing rules as any other page.

terms.summary: A news post is a page that shares an announcement or a story with the people who follow a site. It appears in news feeds and on the SharePoint start page.

levels.beginner: A no-code agent is an AI helper you set up by describing it, without writing programs.
levels.maker: Anyone can create one with instructions and knowledge, which is quick but needs governance.
levels.architect: Typical tools are [[agent-builder]] and [[copilot-studio]]. Limits include the number of tools, control over orchestration and custom logic.

terms.summary: A no-code agent is an AI helper you set up by describing it, without writing programs.

levels.beginner: Non-deterministic output means asking the same question twice can give two different, equally reasonable answers.
levels.maker: Don't expect identical wording each time. For checks, look at whether the substance is right.
levels.architect: Randomness is controlled by settings such as [[temperature]], where exposed. Evaluate on many runs rather than one.

terms.summary: Non-deterministic output means asking the same question twice can give two different, equally reasonable answers.

levels.beginner: A notification is a ping telling you something finished or needs you.
levels.maker: Agents and workflows can alert you when a task is done or waiting for a decision.
levels.architect: Be careful what a notification reveals, since it may display data outside the original security boundary.

terms.summary: A notification is a ping telling you something finished or needs you.

levels.beginner: This is the search engine service of the older Office SharePoint Server product.
levels.maker: It is the farm-wide service that either responds to query requests from front-end web servers or crawls items. It belongs to older on-premises SharePoint.
levels.architect: The service takes one of two roles: answering queries from front-end web servers, or crawling items. It is a [[sharepoint-server]] feature.

terms.summary: This is the search engine service of the older Office SharePoint Server product.

levels.beginner: OneDrive is the personal online storage that comes with a work or school Microsoft 365 account. It is your own private folder in the cloud, and you choose what to share with others.
levels.maker: Behind the scenes a OneDrive works like a SharePoint [[document-library]] that belongs to one person. It syncs to your computer, supports sharing links and versions, and is managed by your admin through quotas and policies. It used to be called OneDrive for Business, so older articles and tools may use that name.
levels.architect: Each user's OneDrive is a personal site collection that is created the first time it is needed. Files are reachable through Microsoft Graph at the user's drive and share the same storage engine as SharePoint libraries. Retention, sharing and quota are governed by tenant policies.

terms.summary: OneDrive is the personal online storage that comes with a work or school Microsoft 365 account. It is your own private folder in the cloud, and you choose what to share with others.

levels.beginner: Open Item permission is the right to open and read a whole file.
levels.maker: It is an authorisation that allows a user to retrieve an entire file. Compare it with [[open-web-permission]].
levels.architect: The permission covers retrieval of an entire file. Permission levels, such as those of [[sharepoint-groups]], build on rights like this.

terms.summary: Open Item permission is the right to open and read a whole file.

levels.beginner: Open web permission is the right to open a site, needed when you export or import it.
levels.maker: It is a requisite permission during the import or export of a SharePoint site. Without it the operation cannot open the site.
levels.architect: The permission is required for import and export. It differs from [[open-item-permission]], which concerns a single file.

terms.summary: Open web permission is the right to open a site, needed when you export or import it.

levels.beginner: An OpenAI model is an AI model made by the company OpenAI.
levels.maker: Microsoft uses OpenAI technology in several Copilot and Azure AI experiences, alongside its own services and controls.
levels.architect: The model is only one layer of the product. Data handling, grounding and safety are provided by Microsoft's services around it.

terms.summary: An OpenAI model is an AI model made by the company OpenAI.

levels.beginner: The operator account is the login of the person running a content import.
levels.maker: It is the account of the user who is managing the import process for a deployment package. See [[content-migration-package]].
levels.architect: Make sure this account has the permissions the import needs, such as [[open-web-permission]].

terms.summary: The operator account is the login of the person running a content import.

levels.beginner: Orchestration is the conductor's job: coordinating the model, the instructions, the lookups and the tools so a task gets done.
levels.maker: It decides what to ask the model, what to retrieve and which tool to call, and in what order.
levels.architect: It covers planning, retrieval, [[tool-calling|tool use]] and multi-step action. The [[orchestrator]] is the component that does this work in an agent.

terms.summary: Orchestration is the conductor's job: coordinating the model, the instructions, the lookups and the tools so a task gets done.

levels.beginner: The orchestrator is the agent's project manager: it decides which information to look up and which tools to use, and in what order, to answer you.
levels.maker: It manages how an [[agent]] works with its knowledge, actions and level of autonomy. In a [[declarative-agent]] Microsoft supplies it, and in a [[custom-engine-agent]] you provide it.
levels.architect: The orchestrator sits between the user experience and the foundation models. It interprets the request, selects context and capabilities, calls tools and asks the [[large-language-model]] to generate the response. It is not a fixed sequence, so the number of retrievals or tool calls varies from one request to the next.

terms.summary: The orchestrator is the agent's project manager: it decides which information to look up and which tools to use, and in what order, to answer you.

levels.beginner: Organisational context is what the AI knows about how your organisation works: roles, relationships, files and activity.
levels.maker: It makes answers more relevant, for example by knowing who your team is.
levels.architect: It is assembled from work data and respects permissions. See [[user-context]] for the person-specific side.

terms.summary: Organisational context is what the AI knows about how your organisation works: roles, relationships, files and activity.

levels.beginner: Organisational data is information your organisation owns or manages.
levels.maker: It includes Microsoft 365 content and approved data from connected business systems.
levels.architect: Classify and label it so that access, retention and AI use follow the right rules.

terms.summary: Organisational data is information your organisation owns or manages.

levels.beginner: Organisational search finds things across your workplace: people, documents, messages and sites.
levels.maker: It only shows what the person is allowed to see.
levels.architect: It rests on a permission-aware index; see [[permission-trimming]] and [[microsoft-search]].

terms.summary: Organisational search finds things across your workplace: people, documents, messages and sites.

levels.beginner: An organization identifier is the unique number that stands for one organisation.
levels.maker: It is an integer that uniquely identifies an organisation.
levels.architect: The identifier is an integer. Use it, not the name, to refer to an organisation in code.

terms.summary: An organization identifier is the unique number that stands for one organisation.

levels.beginner: An orphaned object is something left behind that has lost its parent, like a file in a folder that no longer exists.
levels.maker: It is a content database object that lacks a requisite relationship to a corresponding object. Orphans are usually a sign of a failed or interrupted operation.
levels.architect: The object exists in the content database without the relationship it needs to another object. Look for orphans when a migration or deletion did not finish cleanly.

terms.summary: An orphaned object is something left behind that has lost its parent, like a file in a folder that no longer exists.

levels.beginner: Output is what the AI gives back: text, a decision, a recommendation or an action.
levels.maker: Output depends on the prompt and available context.
levels.architect: Validate output before using it in downstream systems. Outputs that trigger actions need stronger controls.

terms.summary: Output is what the AI gives back: text, a decision, a recommendation or an action.

levels.beginner: Oversight is people keeping an eye on AI systems so they stay useful, safe and on track.
levels.maker: Organisations assign owners and review how AI is used and what it produces.
levels.architect: Oversight spans accountability, monitoring and escalation. It is broader than approving individual outputs, which is [[human-in-the-loop]].

terms.summary: Oversight is people keeping an eye on AI systems so they stay useful, safe and on track.

levels.beginner: A paged view shows a long list a page at a time instead of all at once.
levels.maker: It is a view that supports one or more visual pages. It is used to break large sets of data into smaller sets for better performance and manageability.
levels.architect: Paging breaks big data sets up so that each request returns less. It does not replace the need to plan around the [[list-view-threshold]].

terms.summary: A paged view shows a long list a page at a time instead of all at once.

levels.beginner: A parent farm is the main farm that gathers information from another farm and answers questions about it.
levels.maker: It is a farm that crawls content from another farm and also responds to query requests from that farm.
levels.architect: The parent crawls content from the other farm, and it also serves queries from that farm.

terms.summary: A parent farm is the main farm that gathers information from another farm and answers questions about it.

levels.beginner: A parent list is the list that holds a given item or folder.
levels.maker: It is a list that contains a list item or [[list-folder]]. The item belongs to its parent.
levels.architect: Use it to describe the containment relationship from an item or folder to its [[sharepoint-list]].

terms.summary: A parent list is the list that holds a given item or folder.

levels.beginner: This is a special library that keeps the data connections for PerformancePoint dashboards.
levels.maker: It is a SharePoint [[document-library]] that contains PerformancePoint data sources.
levels.architect: It stores the PerformancePoint data sources as items of a document library, so normal library permissions apply.

terms.summary: This is a special library that keeps the data connections for PerformancePoint dashboards.

levels.beginner: Permission trimming means search and AI only show you what you already have the right to see.
levels.maker: If a file is not shared with you, Copilot should not use it in your answers.
levels.architect: Retrieval filters results against the requesting identity. It does not fix over-shared content, so check permissions before rolling out Copilot.

terms.summary: Permission trimming means search and AI only show you what you already have the right to see.

levels.beginner: A personal site is a person's own space on SharePoint, used for their own work.
levels.maker: It is a type of SharePoint site that is used by an individual user for personal productivity. It appears to the user as My Site. Today, [[onedrive]] fills that role for personal files.
levels.architect: The site is for one person. In current Microsoft 365 the personal file space is [[onedrive]].

terms.summary: A personal site is a person's own space on SharePoint, used for their own work.

levels.beginner: Personalisation is the AI adapting its answers to you: your role, preferences and work habits.
levels.maker: It makes responses more useful but depends on what the AI may use about you.
levels.architect: Check privacy controls and what signals are used.

terms.summary: Personalisation is the AI adapting its answers to you: your role, preferences and work habits.

levels.beginner: The Planner Agent is an AI assistant that helps with project and plan management.
levels.maker: It was called the Project Manager Agent until March 2026. Like other [[agent|agents]], it works within the permissions of the people who use it.
levels.architect: Check what it can read and change before you roll it out, and make sure project data is shared with the right people, since an agent can only work from what its users can access.

terms.summary: The Planner Agent is an AI assistant that helps with project and plan management.

levels.beginner: A plugin is an older name for an add-on that gives an AI assistant extra abilities.
levels.maker: Microsoft's newer agent and tool terms have replaced some earlier plugin-based approaches, so you may see both in older material.
levels.architect: When you see "plugin" in older guidance, check whether the current equivalent is an [[agent-action]], connector or MCP server.

terms.summary: A plugin is an older name for an add-on that gives an AI assistant extra abilities.

levels.beginner: A policy is a rule that says what is and isn't allowed.
levels.maker: Policies can control access, data handling, AI behaviour, security and acceptable use.
levels.architect: Some are technical and enforced by the service, others are guidance. Align them to [[governance]].

terms.summary: A policy is a rule that says what is and isn't allowed.

levels.beginner: Portal content is the main collection of what search has gathered, with its sources and settings.
levels.maker: It is the main search catalog, which contains the content sources and settings that are related to a crawl.
levels.architect: It holds the content sources and settings for the crawl. See also [[search-catalog]].

terms.summary: Portal content is the main collection of what search has gathered, with its sources and settings.

levels.beginner: Power Apps lets people build business apps without being professional programmers, by placing things on a screen and describing behaviour with simple formulas.
levels.maker: There are two main kinds of app. A [[canvas-app]] gives you full control over the layout, and a [[model-driven-app]] is generated from your data in [[dataverse]]. Apps can be shared with colleagues and run in a browser or on a phone.
levels.architect: Apps reach data through [[connector|connectors]] or, for model-driven apps, natively through [[dataverse]]. Logic is written in [[power-fx]]. Package apps in a [[solution]] to move them between [[environment|environments]]. People need access to the app and to every data source it uses.

terms.summary: Power Apps lets people build business apps without being professional programmers, by placing things on a screen and describing behaviour with simple formulas.

levels.beginner: Power Automate lets you set up a chain of steps that runs by itself, such as saving email attachments to a folder or asking a manager to approve a request.
levels.maker: Automations are called flows. A [[cloud-flow]] runs online when something happens or on a schedule, and a [[desktop-flow]] repeats actions on a Windows computer. Flows use [[connector|connectors]] to talk to other services. It used to be called Microsoft Flow, so older articles may say 'Flow' for the whole product.
levels.architect: Flows belong to an [[environment]] and run under a connection's permissions, so a change of owner, a shared connection or licensing can decide whether a flow keeps running. Move flows with [[solution|solutions]] and use [[data-policy|data policies]] to stop risky connector combinations. A model-driven [[business-process-flow]] is authored in the same designer but is a different thing.

terms.summary: Power Automate lets you set up a chain of steps that runs by itself, such as saving email attachments to a folder or asking a manager to approve a request.

levels.beginner: Power BI turns data into charts and reports so people can see what is happening in the business at a glance.
levels.maker: Power BI connects to many data sources, and [[dataverse]] is only one of them. Reports can be embedded in a [[model-driven-app]] or used on their own. Its reports are not stored in Dataverse, and its administration is separate from the Power Platform admin center.
levels.architect: Power BI is made of semantic models, reports and dashboards published to workspaces. Models use import or live connections, and refresh schedules and row-level security are configured in the Power BI service rather than in [[dataverse]].

terms.summary: Power BI turns data into charts and reports so people can see what is happening in the business at a glance.

levels.beginner: Power Fx is the simple formula language used in Power Apps. If you have written a formula in Excel, it will look familiar.
levels.maker: You use Power Fx to say what happens when someone selects a button, how to filter a list, or when to show or hide something. It is also used in other low-code places, such as formulas in [[copilot-studio]]. Because it is formula based, you can read an app's logic without hunting through code.
levels.architect: Power Fx is a declarative, strongly typed, Excel-style language whose formulas recalculate when their inputs change. Microsoft has released the language as open source, and the same formulas can run in different Power Platform hosts. Delegation to the data source decides how much of the work is done server-side.

terms.summary: Power Fx is the simple formula language used in Power Apps. If you have written a formula in Excel, it will look familiar.

levels.beginner: Power Pages is for building websites that people outside your organisation can use, such as a customer portal or a sign-up page, without writing a website from scratch.
levels.maker: You design a site in a visual studio from templates and connect it to the same business data as your apps in [[dataverse]]. It was previously called Power Apps portals. Compare it with a [[communication-site]] in SharePoint, which shares information inside the organisation.
levels.architect: Power Pages is a low-code software-as-a-service platform for external-facing business websites. Site data is stored and secured in [[dataverse]], where web roles and table permissions control what visitors can read or change. Developers can extend sites with Liquid templates and code, and sites move between environments with [[solution|solutions]].

terms.summary: Power Pages is for building websites that people outside your organisation can use, such as a customer portal or a sign-up page, without writing a website from scratch.

levels.beginner: Power Platform is Microsoft's family of low-code tools for building apps, automating work, making websites and analysing data. Think of it as a workshop with a different tool for each job, all sharing the same shelves of data.
levels.maker: The main tools are [[power-apps]] for apps, [[power-automate]] for automation, [[power-pages]] for external websites and [[power-bi]] for reports, and [[copilot-studio]] builds AI agents on the same foundations. They share [[connector|connectors]], [[dataverse]] and [[environment|environments]], so one solution can mix several of them.
levels.architect: Everything is organised by [[environment]]: each one sits in a Microsoft Entra tenant and a geography, and holds apps, flows, agents and data. Teams move work between environments with [[solution|solutions]], and administrators govern it in the [[power-platform-admin-center]], using [[data-policy|data policies]] to control which connectors can be combined.

terms.summary: Power Platform is Microsoft's family of low-code tools for building apps, automating work, making websites and analysing data. Think of it as a workshop with a different tool for each job, all sharing the same shelves of data.

levels.beginner: The Power Platform admin center is the control room where administrators look after environments, settings and policies.
levels.maker: It is a unified portal for managing [[environment|environments]] and settings for Power Apps, Power Automate and Dynamics 365 apps. This is where you create environments, set [[data-policy|data policies]] and check usage. It is separate from the Microsoft 365 admin center.
levels.architect: Administrative actions can also be scripted through the Power Platform CLI, PowerShell and APIs, which is how larger organisations automate environment creation and governance. Administration of [[power-bi]] has its own separate settings.

terms.summary: The Power Platform admin center is the control room where administrators look after environments, settings and policies.

levels.beginner: Preview means a feature is available early and may still change.
levels.maker: Previews may behave differently, have limits and carry different support terms.
levels.architect: Avoid production dependence on previews unless you accept change and limited support. See [[general-availability]].

terms.summary: Preview means a feature is available early and may still change.

levels.beginner: Principal aliasing is a way of saying "this person in one list is the same as that person in another".
levels.maker: It is the process of mapping a user or a group in one [[user-store]] to a user or a group in another. The goal is to return all the documents the user or group may view, regardless of which store they were authenticated against.
levels.architect: The mapping lets security filters cover several stores. It supports [[user-search-security-filter|user search security filters]].

terms.summary: Principal aliasing is a way of saying "this person in one list is the same as that person in another".

levels.beginner: The privacy level decides who is allowed to see your personal details on your profile.
levels.maker: It is a setting that specifies the category of users who are allowed to view the personal information of other users, such as user profile properties, colleagues or memberships.
levels.architect: The setting controls who sees data of the [[user-profile-store]], so check the level when profile data seems to be hidden.

terms.summary: The privacy level decides who is allowed to see your personal details on your profile.

levels.beginner: A prompt is what you type or send to an AI to tell it what you want. A clearer prompt usually gets a better answer.
levels.maker: Good prompts say the task, the context and the format you want. In an [[agent]], the instructions work as a standing prompt that applies to every conversation.
levels.architect: A prompt is assembled from system instructions, retrieved context, conversation history and the user's message. Keep instructions specific and test them against real questions. Content pulled into a prompt can itself contain instructions, so it should not be trusted blindly.

terms.summary: A prompt is what you type or send to an AI to tell it what you want. A clearer prompt usually gets a better answer.

levels.beginner: Prompt chaining splits a big job into a series of smaller asks, each building on the last.
levels.maker: It often gives better results than one huge request.
levels.architect: Each step's output feeds the next. Validate intermediate results to stop errors compounding.

terms.summary: Prompt chaining splits a big job into a series of smaller asks, each building on the last.

levels.beginner: Prompt engineering is the skill of asking the AI in a clear way so the answer is useful.
levels.maker: State the goal, give context and say the format you want.
levels.architect: It includes structuring instructions, examples and constraints and iterating against test cases.

terms.summary: Prompt engineering is the skill of asking the AI in a clear way so the answer is useful.

levels.beginner: A prompt gallery is a library of ready-made questions to try with Copilot.
levels.maker: It helps people learn what good prompts look like.
levels.architect: Organisations may curate their own examples for common tasks.

terms.summary: A prompt gallery is a library of ready-made questions to try with Copilot.

levels.beginner: Prompt injection is sneaking hidden instructions into content so the AI follows the attacker's orders.
levels.maker: A document or web page could contain text that tells the AI to leak data or change its behaviour.
levels.architect: Retrieved content must be treated as untrusted. Mitigate with filtering, limited tool permissions, [[human-in-the-loop]] approval for risky actions and monitoring.

terms.summary: Prompt injection is sneaking hidden instructions into content so the AI follows the attacker's orders.

levels.beginner: Protected material is content covered by copyright or similar protection.
levels.maker: AI tools may need to detect and handle it carefully when producing or changing content.
levels.architect: Check provider guidance and your own policy about reuse of generated text, code and images.

terms.summary: Protected material is content covered by copyright or similar protection.

levels.beginner: Provisioned means that something has been set up and made ready for use.
levels.maker: It describes an object that was created and deployed successfully. A failed set-up would not be provisioned.
levels.architect: Use it as the state of an object that was created and deployed successfully.

terms.summary: Provisioned means that something has been set up and made ready for use.

levels.beginner: The public filter lets search show items that everyone is allowed to see.
levels.maker: It is the search security filter in FAST Search Authorization that finds the documents that all users have access to.
levels.architect: It complements the [[user-search-security-filter]] that is built for each user.

terms.summary: The public filter lets search show items that everyone is allowed to see.

levels.beginner: Publish to server means saving a document, or part of one, to a web server.
levels.maker: It is a process that facilitates saving a document, or portions of a document, to a web server.
levels.architect: The process is the step that puts content on the web server. Compare with the [[published-version]] of a list item.

terms.summary: Publish to server means saving a document, or part of one, to a web server.

levels.beginner: A published version is the approved copy that everyone can see.
levels.maker: It is the version of a list item that is approved and can be seen by all users. The user interface version number is incremented to the next major version, and the minor version is zero. See [[version-history]].
levels.architect: The number moves to the next positive major version and the minor part is zero. The [[publishing-level]] indicates the publishing status of a version.

terms.summary: A published version is the approved copy that everyone can see.

levels.beginner: The publishing level is a number that says where a version is in the publishing process.
levels.maker: It is an integer that is assigned to a document to indicate the publishing status of that version of the document.
levels.architect: The integer shows the publishing status of a version. See [[published-version]] for the approved one.

terms.summary: The publishing level is a number that says where a version is in the publishing process.

levels.beginner: A publishing page is a page built by pouring content into a ready-made layout.
levels.maker: It is a document that binds to a page layout to generate an HTML page for readers. Publishing pages have specific fields containing the content that is displayed. See [[content-placeholder]].
levels.architect: The page binds to a layout, and the fields supply the content shown in the [[content-placeholder|placeholders]]. Compare with a modern [[site-page]].

terms.summary: A publishing page is a page built by pouring content into a ready-made layout.

levels.beginner: Q&A is asking a question and getting an answer.
levels.maker: Copilot finds or works out the answer from relevant information.
levels.architect: Quality depends on retrieval and [[grounding]]; use [[citation|citations]] to verify.

terms.summary: Q&A is asking a question and getting an answer.

levels.beginner: A query is a request for information sent to a search or data service.
levels.maker: Copilot often turns your question into one or more queries behind the scenes.
levels.architect: Query generation and rewriting affect results as much as the index does.

terms.summary: A query is a request for information sent to a search or data service.

levels.beginner: Query expansion adds related words to a search so it finds more relevant things.
levels.maker: For example "car" may also search for "vehicle".
levels.architect: Over-expansion can add noise, so evaluate recall and precision.

terms.summary: Query expansion adds related words to a search so it finds more relevant things.

levels.beginner: Query independent rank is a score for how important an item is, whatever you search for.
levels.maker: It is a system to rank items using features that do not vary with different queries. Contrast with [[dynamic-rank]].
levels.architect: The features it uses do not change with the query. It is closely related to [[static-rank]].

terms.summary: Query independent rank is a score for how important an item is, whatever you search for.

levels.beginner: A query table is a spreadsheet-like table filled with data from another system.
levels.maker: It is a two-dimensional table that presents data from an external data source.
levels.architect: The data is brought in from an external source and shown as rows and columns.

terms.summary: A query table is a spreadsheet-like table filled with data from another system.

levels.beginner: A quick action is a one-click shortcut for a common Copilot task.
levels.maker: It saves you writing a full prompt.
levels.architect: Behind the shortcut is a predefined [[prompt]], so results still depend on context.

terms.summary: A quick action is a one-click shortcut for a common Copilot task.

levels.beginner: A quota is a limit on how much you can use a service.
levels.maker: Limits can apply to requests, capacity or credits for a tenant, agent or user.
levels.architect: Plan for throttling, monitor consumption and know what happens when a limit is reached.

terms.summary: A quota is a limit on how much you can use a service.

levels.beginner: A ranking parameter is a dial that influences which items appear higher in search results.
levels.maker: It is a value that is used to influence the algorithm that determines the rank of an item. See [[dynamic-rank]] and [[static-rank]].
levels.architect: Tuning the value changes how the ranking algorithm weighs items.

terms.summary: A ranking parameter is a dial that influences which items appear higher in search results.

levels.beginner: Reasoning is the AI working out an answer step by step rather than blurting it out.
levels.maker: It helps with complex problems and planning, but takes longer.
levels.architect: Reasoning models spend extra computation on intermediate steps. Check conclusions, as fluent reasoning can still be wrong.

terms.summary: Reasoning is the AI working out an answer step by step rather than blurting it out.

levels.beginner: A recommendation is a suggestion made by AI.
levels.maker: Treat it as advice and check it against your own knowledge before important decisions.
levels.architect: State the basis for the suggestion and keep a human accountable for the decision.

terms.summary: A recommendation is a suggestion made by AI.

levels.beginner: The Recycle Bin is where deleted SharePoint files and items wait before they are gone for good. You can restore your own deleted items from the site's Recycle Bin. If they are removed from there, they move to a second-stage bin that only site collection administrators can restore from.
levels.maker: Deleted items are kept for 93 days in total across both stages, counted from the original deletion. The first stage is the site's Recycle Bin, where people see and restore what they deleted. The second stage is the site collection Recycle Bin, found in site settings by a site collection administrator, who can restore anything deleted from the first stage.
levels.architect: The first-stage bin is per site and per user, and the second-stage bin is per [[site-collection]]. Items in either stage still count toward the site collection's storage. After 93 days the content is permanently deleted, so recovery after that point depends on backup or retention policies rather than on the Recycle Bin.

terms.summary: The Recycle Bin is where deleted SharePoint files and items wait before they are gone for good. You can restore your own deleted items from the site's Recycle Bin. If they are removed from there, they move to a second-stage bin that only site collection administrators can restore from.

levels.beginner: Red teaming is deliberately trying to break an AI system to find its weak spots.
levels.maker: Testers use tricky, hostile or unusual prompts so problems are found before real users find them.
levels.architect: It targets safety and security weaknesses such as [[jailbreak|jailbreaks]] and [[prompt-injection]], and complements ordinary [[evaluation]].

terms.summary: Red teaming is deliberately trying to break an AI system to find its weak spots.

levels.beginner: Researcher is a ready-made Copilot helper for digging into a topic across many sources.
levels.maker: It works through multi-step research and produces structured findings with references.
levels.architect: Quality depends on the sources it can reach and on permissions. See also [[analyst]] and [[deep-research]].

terms.summary: Researcher is a ready-made Copilot helper for digging into a topic across many sources.

levels.beginner: A response is the reply you get back from Copilot or an agent.
levels.maker: It may be an answer, content or a status message.
levels.architect: Responses should be checked, particularly where they drive actions.

terms.summary: A response is the reply you get back from Copilot or an agent.

levels.beginner: Responsible AI means building and using AI fairly, safely and transparently, with someone accountable.
levels.maker: It covers fairness, safety, privacy, security, inclusiveness and accountability.
levels.architect: Put principles into practice with assessments, [[evaluation]], documentation and [[oversight]].

terms.summary: Responsible AI means building and using AI fairly, safely and transparently, with someone accountable.

levels.beginner: Retention is the rule for how long content is kept before it is deleted or reviewed.
levels.maker: It applies to documents, records, chats and audit information, and may apply to AI conversations too.
levels.architect: Align retention settings with legal and business needs, as they affect what can be found and recovered.

terms.summary: Retention is the rule for how long content is kept before it is deleted or reviewed.

levels.beginner: Retrieval is the AI looking up relevant information before it answers.
levels.maker: It gets the right passages from search indexes, knowledge sources or connected systems.
levels.architect: Retrieval quality limits answer quality. Combine [[keyword-search]], [[semantic-search]] and [[permission-trimming]].

terms.summary: Retrieval is the AI looking up relevant information before it answers.

levels.beginner: Risk management is spotting what could go wrong with AI and deciding what to do about it.
levels.maker: Risks include security, privacy, legal, operational and accuracy issues.
levels.architect: Assess, treat and monitor each risk and assign an owner.

terms.summary: Risk management is spotting what could go wrong with AI and deciding what to do about it.

levels.beginner: A role identifier is the unique number of a role, such as a permission level, within a site.
levels.maker: It is an integer that uniquely identifies a role definition within a site.
levels.architect: The integer is unique within a site. It differs from the [[role-type]], which is a predefined role definition.

terms.summary: A role identifier is the unique number of a role, such as a permission level, within a site.

levels.beginner: A role type is one of the standard permission sets that come ready-made.
levels.maker: It is a predefined role definition. See [[role-identifier]] for the number that identifies a role within a site.
levels.architect: Predefined role definitions are the basis for permission levels, which are assigned to [[sharepoint-groups]].

terms.summary: A role type is one of the standard permission sets that come ready-made.

levels.beginner: Role-based access control gives people rights according to their job role instead of one by one.
levels.maker: An admin role has admin rights, a reader role has read rights.
levels.architect: Define roles narrowly and review membership. It supports [[least-privilege]].

terms.summary: Role-based access control gives people rights according to their job role instead of one by one.

levels.beginner: A root document is a file that sits at the very top level of a site, not inside a folder.
levels.maker: It is a document in the root folder of a site.
levels.architect: The document lives directly in the site's root folder rather than in a library.

terms.summary: A root document is a file that sits at the very top level of a site, not inside a folder.

levels.beginner: Safe completion is an AI staying helpful while steering clear of unsafe requests.
levels.maker: Rather than just refusing, it may redirect or give a safer answer.
levels.architect: It is a model behaviour pattern, complementing external [[guardrail|guardrails]].

terms.summary: Safe completion is an AI staying helpful while steering clear of unsafe requests.

levels.beginner: Scheduled means an item has a set date and time for going live or being taken down.
levels.maker: It is a status applied to a list item or document that specifies a time when the item or document will be published or unpublished.
levels.architect: The status is set on the item. It states a time at which the item is published or unpublished.

terms.summary: Scheduled means an item has a set date and time for going live or being taken down.

levels.beginner: The schema version is the edition number of the rule sheet that a deployment package follows.
levels.maker: It is an integer value that represents the version number of the schema for a deployment package. See [[content-migration-package]].
levels.architect: The integer identifies the schema that the package uses. Check it when a package fails to import.

terms.summary: The schema version is the edition number of the rule sheet that a deployment package follows.

levels.beginner: A search application is one self-contained set of search settings.
levels.maker: It is a unique group of search settings that is associated, one to one, with a shared service provider. It is the home of the [[search-catalog]].
levels.architect: Each search application pairs with a shared service provider. Its crawl data lives in the [[search-catalog]].

terms.summary: A search application is one self-contained set of search settings.

levels.beginner: The search catalog is the big collection of facts that search gathered, used to answer your questions.
levels.maker: It is all of the crawl data that is associated with a given [[search-application]]. It provides the information used to generate the query results.
levels.architect: The catalog is what queries read from. Its data is generated by crawling.

terms.summary: The search catalog is the big collection of facts that search gathered, used to answer your questions.

levels.beginner: The search database is where search keeps its notes, in a database.
levels.maker: It is a database that stores search-related information, including stored procedures and tables used for crawler data, document metadata and administration information.
levels.architect: It holds the crawler data, document metadata and administration information. Do not confuse it with the [[search-catalog]].

terms.summary: The search database is where search keeps its notes, in a database.

levels.beginner: The search query log is a record of what people searched for and when.
levels.maker: It is a record of information about user searches, such as search terms and the time of access. It helps administrators understand what people look for.
levels.architect: Use the log to see which terms people search for. The log records search terms and time of access.

terms.summary: The search query log is a record of what people searched for and when.

levels.beginner: A search scope consumer is a site collection that uses a particular menu of search areas.
levels.maker: It is a site collection that uses a particular [[search-scope-display-group]].
levels.architect: The consumer is a [[site-collection]] that picks one display group of scopes.

terms.summary: A search scope consumer is a site collection that uses a particular menu of search areas.

levels.beginner: A search scope display group is a menu that lists the search areas people can choose from.
levels.maker: It is an ordered set of search scopes, defined by an administrator or by code, used to return groups of search scopes. They are saved for each search scope consumer, and a scope can be in several groups.
levels.architect: Groups are saved for each [[search-scope-consumer]]. A search scope can appear in more than one group, and a [[default-search-scope]] is assigned automatically.

terms.summary: A search scope display group is a menu that lists the search areas people can choose from.

levels.beginner: The search scope index is a speed-up for searches that are limited to a scope.
levels.maker: It is a specialised component of a full-text index catalog that is built on the values of scoped properties for optimised queries.
levels.architect: It is built on the values of scoped properties. It sits alongside the [[full-text-index-component]].

terms.summary: The search scope index is a speed-up for searches that are limited to a scope.

levels.beginner: A search scope rule decides what is included in a search area.
levels.maker: It is an attribute that specifies which items are included in a given search scope.
levels.architect: The rule determines membership of the scope. The [[contextual-search-scope]] is a system-defined scope added to a query.

terms.summary: A search scope rule decides what is included in a search area.

levels.beginner: The search service account is the login the search service runs under.
levels.maker: It is a user account under which the search service runs.
levels.architect: Give the account the rights search needs and no more, since it is used to run the service.

terms.summary: The search service account is the login the search service runs under.

levels.beginner: This is the object that holds the settings shared by a search application.
levels.maker: It is an instance of a shared application for search that holds search-specific settings. See [[search-application]].
levels.architect: The object holds search-specific settings for the shared application.

terms.summary: This is the object that holds the settings shared by a search application.

levels.beginner: A security role is a set of permissions, like a job badge that says which doors a person can open and what they can do inside.
levels.maker: In Dataverse a role says what people can see and do, such as create, read, write, delete, update or append rows in a [[dataverse-table]]. People are placed in roles, often through security groups. Give people the smallest role that lets them do their job.
levels.architect: Roles hold privileges per table at different access levels, and a person's effective access combines all of their roles. Roles belong to an [[environment]] and can be shipped in a [[solution]]. Compare them with SharePoint's [[sharepoint-groups]], which control access to sites rather than to data rows.

terms.summary: A security role is a set of permissions, like a job badge that says which doors a person can open and what they can do inside.

levels.beginner: A semantic index is a search catalogue that understands meaning, not just words.
levels.maker: It helps Copilot find relevant content even if the wording differs.
levels.architect: It is built from [[embedding|embeddings]] and relationships in organisational content and respects [[permission-trimming]].

terms.summary: A semantic index is a search catalogue that understands meaning, not just words.

levels.beginner: Semantic search finds results by meaning and intent, not just matching words.
levels.maker: Typing "how do I get paid back for travel" can find the expenses policy.
levels.architect: Usually uses [[embedding|embeddings]] and [[vector-search]], often combined with [[keyword-search]].

terms.summary: Semantic search finds results by meaning and intent, not just matching words.

levels.beginner: A sensitivity label is a tag on a file saying how confidential it is and how it must be handled.
levels.maker: Labels can add protections such as encryption and restrict who can access content.
levels.architect: Managed in [[microsoft-purview]]. AI output can inherit or reflect labels, so make sure labels are applied consistently.

terms.summary: A sensitivity label is a tag on a file saying how confidential it is and how it must be handled.

levels.beginner: The server-to-server protocol is how two servers prove who they are to each other.
levels.maker: It is an authentication protocol between two servers or services. It is used by a [[high-trust-app]], and the add-in model that relies on it is retired in SharePoint Online.
levels.architect: Two servers or services authenticate each other with the protocol. A [[high-trust-app]] uses it and builds the user part of the token itself.

terms.summary: The server-to-server protocol is how two servers prove who they are to each other.

levels.beginner: A session is one stretch of interaction with Copilot or an agent.
levels.maker: It holds related prompts and replies and some temporary state.
levels.architect: Session state ends or expires, so don't rely on it for long-term storage.

terms.summary: A session is one stretch of interaction with Copilot or an agent.

levels.beginner: Shadow AI is AI tools people use at work without the organisation's approval or knowledge.
levels.maker: It can leak data or break rules because nobody is overseeing it.
levels.architect: Reduce it by offering approved tools, clear [[policy|policies]] and visibility.

terms.summary: Shadow AI is AI tools people use at work without the organisation's approval or knowledge.

levels.beginner: The Shared Documents library is the ready-made folder for files that comes with a new team site.
levels.maker: It is a [[document-library]] that is included by default in the Team Site template. See [[team-site]].
levels.architect: The library is created by default with the Team Site site template.

terms.summary: The Shared Documents library is the ready-made folder for files that comes with a new team site.

levels.beginner: A shared view is a way of looking at a list that everyone allowed to see it can use.
levels.maker: It is a view of a list or web part page that every user with the appropriate permissions can see. A personal view, by contrast, is for one person.
levels.architect: Anyone with the appropriate permissions sees the same view. See also [[default-list-view]].

terms.summary: A shared view is a way of looking at a list that everyone allowed to see it can use.

levels.beginner: SharePoint Add-ins are an older way to give SharePoint sites extra features, using small apps installed on a site. In SharePoint Online they stopped working on 2 April 2026, and newer extras are built with the SharePoint Framework instead.
levels.maker: Add-ins stopped working in SharePoint Online on 2 April 2026. Anything that still depends on one must be rebuilt, usually with the [[spfx]]. The model still exists for on-premises SharePoint Server. When you search an old name such as "app for SharePoint", this is the term you land on.
levels.architect: An add-in runs in an isolated [[app-web]] (SharePoint-hosted) or on an external host (provider-hosted), and works against the [[host-web]] it is installed on. Their authentication relied on Azure Access Control Services, which is also being retired. Plan migrations by inventorying installed add-ins in the [[app-catalog]], then re-implementing each as a solution built with the [[spfx]] or as a service that uses Microsoft Graph.

terms.summary: SharePoint Add-ins are an older way to give SharePoint sites extra features, using small apps installed on a site. In SharePoint Online they stopped working on 2 April 2026, and newer extras are built with the SharePoint Framework instead.

levels.beginner: The SharePoint Framework, or SPFx, is the modern way for developers to build custom extras for SharePoint, such as new page building blocks, that run safely inside SharePoint pages.
levels.maker: With SPFx developers build [[web-part|web parts]], extensions that customise pages, lists and the toolbar, and Viva Connections cards. You get them as a package that an admin or site owner adds from the [[app-catalog]]. SPFx is the supported replacement for [[sharepoint-add-in|SharePoint Add-ins]].
levels.architect: SPFx runs client-side in the page context under the signed-in user's permissions. It is written in TypeScript with any modern UI library and built with a Node.js toolchain into an .sppkg package. Solutions call SharePoint REST, Microsoft Graph and Entra-secured APIs. Packages are deployed through the [[app-catalog]], tenant-wide or per site collection, and the same web parts can also appear as Teams tabs.

terms.summary: The SharePoint Framework, or SPFx, is the modern way for developers to build custom extras for SharePoint, such as new page building blocks, that run safely inside SharePoint pages.

levels.beginner: SharePoint groups are the permission buckets of a site. Owners can do everything, Members can add and edit, and Visitors can only read.
levels.maker: Every [[sharepoint-site]] has these three groups, and you give access by adding people to the right one. Libraries, lists and items inherit the site's permissions unless someone breaks the inheritance. On a [[team-site]] connected to a Microsoft 365 group, the group's owners and members are mapped to the site's Owners and Members.
levels.architect: Each group is granted a permission level on the site: Full Control, Edit and Read by default. Breaking inheritance on many items is costly because every item then carries its own permissions, so prefer fewer, broader groups and security groups over individual grants. Do not mix up SharePoint groups with Microsoft 365 groups, which also control a team's mailbox and Teams membership.

terms.summary: SharePoint groups are the permission buckets of a site. Owners can do everything, Members can add and edit, and Visitors can only read.

levels.beginner: A SharePoint list is a table of information, such as tasks, issues, contacts or equipment, that everyone with access can view and update. Each row is an item and each column holds one kind of detail.
levels.maker: Start from a template or from scratch, then add columns, views, filters and column formatting. Lists connect well to Power Automate flows and Power Apps forms. The Microsoft Lists app gives you a personal home for lists across sites. A [[document-library]] is a list that holds files.
levels.architect: A list (SPList) stores items with fields defined by [[site-column|site columns]] or by columns local to the list. Item-level permissions are possible but should be used sparingly. Data is available through REST, Microsoft Graph and CSOM. Lists support up to 30 million items, with the list view threshold of 5,000 applying to unindexed queries.

terms.summary: A SharePoint list is a table of information, such as tasks, issues, contacts or equipment, that everyone with access can view and update. Each row is an item and each column holds one kind of detail.

levels.beginner: SharePoint Online is the cloud version of SharePoint that comes with Microsoft 365. Microsoft runs the servers for you, so there is nothing to install or look after.
levels.maker: It receives new features continuously and is where modern sites, [[hub-site|hubs]], the [[spfx]] and Microsoft Lists live. Your organisation manages it through the SharePoint admin center rather than by looking after servers. The version you run yourself is [[sharepoint-server]].
levels.architect: A multitenant service: each organisation has a tenant with its own sites, storage quotas and policies. Customisation is client-side, through the [[spfx]], Microsoft Graph and the REST APIs, because server-side code such as a [[farm-solution]] cannot run there. Calls are subject to throttling, so batch work and back off when asked to.

terms.summary: SharePoint Online is the cloud version of SharePoint that comes with Microsoft 365. Microsoft runs the servers for you, so there is nothing to install or look after.

levels.beginner: This is a way to write a search question in the style of a database query.
levels.maker: It is the set of rules that govern how an enterprise search SQL query is built.
levels.architect: The syntax governs how an enterprise search SQL query is constructed. Modern search favours other query languages.

terms.summary: This is a way to write a search question in the style of a database query.

levels.beginner: SharePoint Server is the version of SharePoint that an organisation installs and runs on its own servers, instead of using Microsoft's cloud.
levels.maker: Because your own team runs it, you choose when to update it and where the data sits. It is also called on-premises SharePoint. The current release is SharePoint Server Subscription Edition, and it receives fewer new features than [[sharepoint-online]]. Many organisations run both and connect them in a hybrid setup.
levels.architect: It runs as a farm of web, application and database servers, with SQL Server holding the content. Full-trust code such as a [[farm-solution]] is possible, and so are [[sharepoint-add-in|SharePoint Add-ins]]. Customisations that must move to the cloud need to be rebuilt with the [[spfx]] or Microsoft Graph.

terms.summary: SharePoint Server is the version of SharePoint that an organisation installs and runs on its own servers, instead of using Microsoft's cloud.

levels.beginner: A SharePoint site is a website inside Microsoft 365 where a team or organisation keeps its files, news, lists and pages in one place. Think of it as a shared online room: it has its own address, its own furniture (files and lists) and its own guest list (who may come in).
levels.maker: Every site has its own address, permissions, navigation and pages. Modern sites come in two main kinds, the [[team-site]] and the [[communication-site]], and related sites can be tied together with a [[hub-site]]. Inside a site you create [[document-library|libraries]] and [[sharepoint-list|lists]] to hold your content.
levels.architect: A site (the web, or SPWeb) is the container for lists, libraries, pages and permission settings. Each site lives inside a [[site-collection]]. Modern sites are created as the top-level site of their own site collection, and the recommended structure is flat sites joined by hubs rather than nested subsites.

terms.summary: A SharePoint site is a website inside Microsoft 365 where a team or organisation keeps its files, news, lists and pages in one place. Think of it as a shared online room: it has its own address, its own furniture (files and lists) and its own guest list (who may come in).

levels.beginner: A sharing link is a web address you create to give someone access to a file or folder in SharePoint or OneDrive. The type of link decides who can use it.
levels.maker: You can choose between a link that works for anyone, one for people in your organisation, one for people who already have access, and one for specific people. Links can allow viewing or editing, and may have an expiry date. Admins can switch off the types they do not want, for the whole organisation or for a single site.
levels.architect: Creating a link adds a permission grant, backed by a hidden sharing-links group on the site. Many links on many items can therefore build up unique permissions and slow permission checks. Tenant and site sharing settings cap what users can create, and links can also be created with Microsoft Graph. Reviewing and expiring links is part of governance.

terms.summary: A sharing link is a web address you create to give someone access to a file or folder in SharePoint or OneDrive. The type of link decides who can use it.

levels.beginner: Single sign-on lets you sign in once and use many apps.
levels.maker: It saves repeated passwords and makes access easier to manage.
levels.architect: Provided by identity services such as [[microsoft-entra-id]].

terms.summary: Single sign-on lets you sign in once and use many apps.

levels.beginner: A single sign-on ticket is like a stamped pass, so you don't have to show your ID again at every door.
levels.maker: It is a token that contains the encrypted identity of a single sign-on (SSO) user in the form of a security identifier string and a nonce.
levels.architect: The token carries the encrypted identity as a security identifier string and a nonce. Treat it as a credential.

terms.summary: A single sign-on ticket is like a stamped pass, so you don't have to show your ID again at every door.

levels.beginner: A site collection is a group of SharePoint sites that share one top-level site and one set of settings. Think of a building: the building has shared rules and storage, and each room is a site inside it.
levels.maker: Site collections share settings such as storage limits, site collection administrators and the second-stage [[recycle-bin]]. In modern SharePoint every new [[team-site]] or [[communication-site]] gets its own site collection, so in practice each modern site is the only site in its collection.
levels.architect: A site collection (SPSite) is a security and administration boundary. It has one root web and optionally child webs (SPWeb). Features, site collection administrators, quotas, the second-stage recycle bin and the content type gallery are scoped to it. Prefer many small site collections joined by [[hub-site|hubs]] over one large collection with nested subsites.

terms.summary: A site collection is a group of SharePoint sites that share one top-level site and one set of settings. Think of a building: the building has shared rules and storage, and each room is a site inside it.

levels.beginner: A site collection administrator is the person who is in charge of a whole group of sites.
levels.maker: It is a user who has administrative permissions for a [[site-collection]]. It is narrower than the farm-wide role of the [[farm-administrators-group]].
levels.architect: The role covers one site collection only. Farm-level rights belong to the [[farm-administrators-group]].

terms.summary: A site collection administrator is the person who is in charge of a whole group of sites.

levels.beginner: A site collection flag is a set of on-off switches that describe a whole group of sites.
levels.maker: It is a 4-byte unsigned integer bit mask that specifies the properties global to a site collection. One or more values can be set.
levels.architect: Read it as a bit mask. It applies to the whole [[site-collection]], while a [[site-flag]] is for one site.

terms.summary: A site collection flag is a set of on-off switches that describe a whole group of sites.

levels.beginner: A site collection identifier is the unique code of a site collection.
levels.maker: It is a GUID that identifies a [[site-collection]]. In stored procedures it is typically @SiteId or @webSiteId, and in databases SiteId or tp_SiteId.
levels.architect: The GUID names the site collection. Do not confuse it with the [[site-identifier]], which names a site in the collection.

terms.summary: A site collection identifier is the unique code of a site collection.

levels.beginner: A site collection quota is a size limit that stops a group of sites growing without end.
levels.maker: It is an option for a [[site-collection]] that lets administrators set levels for the maximum storage allowed, the maximum number of users allowed, and warnings linked to those maximums.
levels.architect: Administrators can set maximums for storage and for the number of users, and warnings for each of them.

terms.summary: A site collection quota is a size limit that stops a group of sites growing without end.

levels.beginner: A site column is a reusable piece of information, such as "Project owner" or "Due date", that you define once and can then use in many lists and libraries on a site.
levels.maker: Define a site column once, with its type (text, choice, person, date and so on), and add it to a [[content-type]] or directly to lists and libraries. This keeps names and settings consistent. A column created inside a single list is a list column and is not shared.
levels.architect: A site column is a field defined at web scope. Its internal name is fixed when it is created and shows up in code and URLs, so choose it carefully (a display name with spaces becomes encoded, for example _x0020_). Content types reference site columns by ID, and the schema is available through REST and CSOM.

terms.summary: A site column is a reusable piece of information, such as "Project owner" or "Due date", that you define once and can then use in many lists and libraries on a site.

levels.beginner: A site definition is a family of blueprints for sites.
levels.maker: It is a family of site definition configurations. Each site definition specifies a name and contains a list of its [[site-definition-configuration|configurations]].
levels.architect: A definition is a name plus a list of configurations. It differs from a [[site-template]] built from settings.

terms.summary: A site definition is a family of blueprints for sites.

levels.beginner: A site definition configuration is one complete blueprint for a type of site.
levels.maker: It is an XML-based definition of lists, features, modules and other data that together define a type of site. They are stored in the ONET.xml file.
levels.architect: The XML is stored in ONET.xml and defines lists, features, modules and more.

terms.summary: A site definition configuration is one complete blueprint for a type of site.

levels.beginner: The site definition version is the edition number of a site blueprint.
levels.maker: It is a zero-based integer that indicates the version number of the [[site-definition]]. It is suggested that the number is raised each time a definition is updated.
levels.architect: The value is a zero-based integer. Increase it with every update to the definition.

terms.summary: The site definition version is the edition number of a site blueprint.

levels.beginner: A site flag is a set of on-off switches that describe one site.
levels.maker: It is a 4-byte unsigned integer bit mask that specifies properties unique to a site. Compare it with the [[site-collection-flag]].
levels.architect: The mask applies to one site. The [[site-collection-flag]] is global to the collection.

terms.summary: A site flag is a set of on-off switches that describe one site.

levels.beginner: A site identifier is the unique code of a single site.
levels.maker: It is a GUID that identifies a site within a [[site-collection]]. It is also called the web identifier.
levels.architect: The GUID identifies the site in a collection. See the [[site-collection-identifier]] for the collection.

terms.summary: A site identifier is the unique code of a single site.

levels.beginner: The site map is the menu of a model-driven app: it decides which sections and pages people can click in the navigation.
levels.maker: It organises navigation into areas, groups and subareas, where subareas usually open a table's views. Apps with more than one area show a switch at the lower left. The app designer lets you edit it visually.
levels.architect: The site map defines the tables and pages included in a [[model-driven-app]] and the navigation that users get. Because it is app metadata, it ships in a [[solution]] with the app. Older designers edited it as XML; the modern app designer replaces that.

terms.summary: The site map is the menu of a model-driven app: it decides which sections and pages people can click in the navigation.

levels.beginner: Site membership means you belong to a site and have been given a set of rights on it.
levels.maker: It is the status of being a member of a site and having a defined set of user rights to access or manage the content. Groups such as [[members-group]] give the rights.
levels.architect: Rights are granted through groups. See [[sharepoint-groups]].

terms.summary: Site membership means you belong to a site and have been given a set of rights on it.

levels.beginner: A site page is a web page inside a SharePoint site. You build it by adding sections and blocks of content, such as text, images and lists.
levels.maker: You edit a page in the page editor, add sections and columns, and place [[web-part|web parts]] in them. Saving keeps a draft and publishing makes it visible. A [[news-post]] is a special kind of site page. Older wiki and web part pages still exist but are classic.
levels.architect: Modern pages are items in the Site Pages library. Their layout is stored as canvas content that lists sections, columns and the web parts, with each web part's properties. Pages can be created and published through the SharePoint REST API and Microsoft Graph, and custom web parts built with the [[spfx]] appear in the same canvas.

terms.summary: A site page is a web page inside a SharePoint site. You build it by adding sections and blocks of content, such as text, images and lists.

levels.beginner: A site property is a named fact about a site, such as its title or default language.
levels.maker: It is a name and value pair of strings that serves as metadata for a site, such as the title or the default language.
levels.architect: Both name and value are strings. Use properties for small pieces of site metadata.

terms.summary: A site property is a named fact about a site, such as its title or default language.

levels.beginner: A site solution is a ready-to-install package of extras that can be switched on for individual sites.
levels.maker: It is a package that can be deployed and reused that contains a set of features, site definitions and assemblies that apply to sites and can be enabled or disabled individually. It differs from a [[farm-solution]].
levels.architect: It contains features, site definitions and assemblies. See the [[spfx]] for a current model.

terms.summary: A site solution is a ready-to-install package of extras that can be switched on for individual sites.

levels.beginner: A site template is a saved starting point for new sites.
levels.maker: It is an XML-based definition of site settings, including formatting, lists, views and elements such as text, graphics, page layout and styles. Site templates are stored in .stp files in the content database.
levels.architect: The template is XML-based and stored in .stp files. See [[available-site-template]] for the templates people can choose.

terms.summary: A site template is a saved starting point for new sites.

levels.beginner: A skill is a reusable ability you can hand to an agent, like giving a helper a new instruction card.
levels.maker: It is a packaged set of instructions or capabilities that can be added to an [[agent]] so it can do a particular kind of work. Packaging means several agents can share the same skill.
levels.architect: Skills differ from a single [[agent-action]], which performs one operation. A skill can bundle guidance and several steps. Review what a skill can reach before adding it, as it extends what the agent is able to do.

terms.summary: A skill is a reusable ability you can hand to an agent, like giving a helper a new instruction card.

levels.beginner: A solution is a box that you pack your apps and flows into so you can carry them from one environment to another.
